As it is, I’m no longer the one who does these things. It’s the sin living in me that does them.
I know there’s nothing good in my desires that are controlled by sin. I want to do what’s good, but I can’t.
I don’t do the good things I want to do. I keep on doing the evil things I don’t want to do.
So if I do what I don’t want to do, then I’m not the one who’s doing it. It’s the sin living in me that does it.
Here’s the law that I find to be at work in me. When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.
Deep inside I want to follow God’s law.
But I recognize that there’s another law at work inside of me. It’s fighting the law of my mind and making me a prisoner to the law of sin that’s at work within me.
What a terrible situation I’m in! Who will save me from this sin that brings death to my body?
Thanks be to God, who saves me through Jesus Christ our Lord. So in my mind, I’m a slave to God’s law. But if I follow my sinful desires, then I’m a slave to the law of sin.

verses.heading: The Holy Spirit Gives Life / The Holy Spirit Gives Life
verses.text: Therefore, those who belong to Christ Jesus are no longer under God’s judgment.
The law of the Spirit who gives life through Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death.

God did what the written law was not able to do, since it was weakened by our sinful desires. God sent his Son to be an offering for sin. He sent him in human form like those who are susceptible to sin. When God did this, he passed judgment against sin so that it could no longer control people through their wrong desires.
Instead, we are now able to do all the right things that the law requires, because we’re not controlled by those desires. We’re controlled by the Spirit.
Those who do live under the control of their wrong desires think about what sin wants. But those who live under the control of the Spirit think about what the Spirit wants.
If a person’s mind is ruled by their wrong desires, that brings death. But if a person’s mind is ruled by the Spirit, that brings life and peace.
The mind that’s ruled by wrong desires is at war with God. It doesn’t obey God’s law, because it can’t.
Those who are under the power of their desires can’t please God.
If the Spirit of God truly does live in you, you’re not ruled by your desires—you’re ruled by the Spirit. Anyone who doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ doesn’t belong to Christ.
But if Christ lives in you, then even though your body will die because of sin, the Spirit will give you life because you’ve been made right with God.
If the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, then the one who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your bodies because of his Spirit who lives in you.
Brothers and sisters, we have a duty to not live the way our wrong desires would lead us.
If you live that way, you’ll die. But if, by the Spirit’s power, you put to death the wrong things people do in their bodies, then you will live.
All who are led by the Spirit of God are the children of God.

The Spirit you received doesn’t make you slaves who live in fear again. Instead, the Spirit you received has made you God’s genuine child by adoption. And the Spirit leads us to call out to God, “Abba, Father.”
verses.html: The Spirit you received doesn’t make you slaves who live in fear again. Instead, the Spirit you received has made you God’s genuine child by adoption. And the Spirit leads us to call out to God, “Abba, Father.”

verses.text: The Spirit himself joins with our spirits to assure us that we are God’s children.
And since we are his children, we’re going to inherit everything that Christ will also inherit. But we must share in his sufferings if we also want to share in his glory.

verses.heading: Suffering Now and Glory in the Future / Suffering Now and Glory in the Future
verses.text: What we’re suffering now isn’t even worth comparing with the glory that’s coming in the future.
Everything God created is looking forward to the time when his children will appear in their full and final glory.
The created world was held back from fulfilling its purpose, not because it chose that, but because the one who held it back planned things that way. God wanted
creation to live in the hope that it would be set free from decay and enter into the same freedom and glory that his children have.
We know that right up to the present time, the whole creation has been groaning as if it were giving birth to a child.
And that’s not all. We have the first signs of what the Spirit will give us fully, but we also are groaning inside as we wait for our adoption to be finalized.
We can foresee the time when God will set our bodies free. That’s the hope we had when we were saved.
But hope that can be seen isn’t really hope at all. Who hopes for what they already have? But if we hope for what we don’t have yet, we wait for it patiently.
In the same way, the Holy Spirit helps us when we are weak. We don’t know what we should pray for, but the Spirit himself prays for us with groans that are too deep for words.
God, who looks into our hearts, knows the mind of the Spirit, and the Spirit prays for God’s people just as God wants him to pray.
We know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who are called according to his purpose.
God planned that those he already knew ahead of time would become like his Son. In that way, Christ would become the first and most honored among many brothers and sisters.
God made these plans for people to become like his Son, and he called those people to be saved. Then he made those people right with himself, and finally, he them gave his glory.

verses.heading: We Are More Than Conquerors / We Are More Than Conquerors
verses.text: What should we say then? Since God is on our side, who can stand against us?
God didn’t spare his own Son; instead, he gave him up for all of us. How will God not also, along with his Son, freely give us all things?
Who can bring any charge against God’s chosen ones? It’s God who makes us right with himself.
Then who can say we’re guilty? No one. Christ Jesus, who died for us—indeed, who was raised for us—is at the right hand of God praying for us.
Who can separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble or hard times or harm or hunger or nakedness or danger or war?
It is written, “Because of you, we face death all day long. We’re regarded as sheep to be slaughtered.”
No! In all these things we are more than conquerors through Christ who loved us.
I’m convinced that nothing will ever be able to separate us from God’s love—not death or life, angels or demons, the present or the future, and no powers,
heights, or depths, or anything else in all creation. That’s all because of what Christ Jesus our Lord has done.

verses.heading: Paul Mourns for Israel / Paul Mourns for Israel
verses.text: I don’t want any of you to think that I’m not concerned about the people of Israel. They’re my family, my own flesh and blood. (I’m not lying, I’m telling you the truth as one in Christ—my conscience and the Holy Spirit confirm it.)
I’m very sad and I’m constantly distressed about them.
I’m even willing to be cursed and separated from Christ if that would help them.
They’ve been adopted as God’s children. God’s glory belongs to them, and so do the covenants. They received the law and they were taught to worship in the temple. They were given the promises,
and the founders of our nation belong to them. The Messiah comes from their family line. He is God over all. May he be praised forever! Amen.

verses.heading: God’s Free Choice / God’s Free Choice
verses.text: But it’s not as if God’s word has failed. Not everyone in the family line of Israel really belongs to Israel.
Not everyone in Abraham’s family line is his child. On the contrary, Scripture says, “Your family line will continue through Isaac.”

In other words, God’s children aren’t all those who are physically descended from Abraham. Rather, they’re the children God promised to him. Those are the ones who are considered to be Abraham’s children.
God put it this way to Abraham: “I will return at the appointed time and Sarah will have a son.”
And that’s not all. Rebekah’s children were born at the same time, and they had the same father, Isaac.

But even before her twins were born, before they’d done anything good or bad, Rebekah was told, “The older son will serve the younger one.” This shows that God’s purpose was based firmly on his own choice, not on anything the children did.
As it is written, “I chose Jacob instead of Esau.”
What should we say then? Is God unfair? Not at all!
He said to Moses, “I’ll show mercy to those I show mercy to, and I’ll pity the ones I pity.”
So it doesn’t depend on what people want or what they do. It depends on God’s mercy.
In Scripture, God says to Pharaoh, “I had a special reason for making you king. I decided to use you to show my power so that my name would become known everywhere on earth.”
So God does what he wants to do. He shows mercy to one person and makes another person stubborn.
One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still blame us? Who can oppose what he wants to do?”
But who are you, a mere human being, to talk back to God? “Can a clay pot say to the one who made it, ‘Why did you make me like this?’ ”
Isn’t the potter free to make different kinds of pots out of the same lump of clay, some for special purposes and others for ordinary use?
What if God had chosen to show his anger and demonstrate his power, but he was still very patient with the people who were prepared to be destroyed?
What if he did this to show the riches of his glory to the people he had mercy on, the ones he’d prepared to receive his glory?
We are those people. He has chosen us not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles. As
God says in Hosea, “I will call those who are not my people, ‘my people.’ I will call the one who is not my loved one, ‘my loved one.’ ”
He also says, “Where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ there they will be called ‘children of the living God.’ ”
Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, “The number of people from Israel may be like the sand by the sea, but only a few of them will be saved.
The Lord will carry out his sentence on earth quickly, once and for all.”
Just as Isaiah said earlier, “If the Lord Almighty hadn’t left us children and grandchildren, we would have become like Sodom, we would have been like Gomorrah.”

verses.heading: Israel Does Not Believe / Israel Does Not Believe
verses.text: What should we say then? The Gentiles did not look for a way to be right with God, but they found it by having faith.
The people of Israel tried to become right with God by obeying the law, but that didn’t work.
Why not? Because they tried to do it themselves, instead of relying on faith in God. They tripped over the stone that causes people to trip and fall.
As it is written, “Look! I’m laying a stone in Zion that will cause people to trip. It’s a rock that will make them fall. The one who believes in him will never be put to shame.”
Brothers and sisters, with all my heart I long and pray to God for the people of Israel to be saved.
I know for a fact that they want to serve God. But their desire isn’t well informed.
They didn’t know how God makes people right with himself, so they tried to get right with God in their own way. They didn’t realize that
Christ has fulfilled everything the law was meant to do, so now there may be righteousness for everyone who believes.
Moses writes about how the law could help a person do what God requires: “The person who does these things will live by them.”
But doing what God requires starts with having faith in him. Scripture says, “Don’t say in your heart, ‘Who will go up into heaven?’ ” (That means to go up into heaven and bring Christ down.)
“And don’t say, ‘Who will go down into the grave?’ ” (That means to bring Christ up from the dead.)
But what does it say? “The message is near you, it’s in your mouth and in your heart.” (This means the message about faith that we are preaching.)
If you say with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and if you believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
With your heart you believe and are made right with God, and with your mouth you say what you believe. And so you are saved.
Scripture says, “The one who believes in him will never be put to shame.”
There isn’t any difference between Jews and Gentiles; the same Lord is Lord of all, and he richly blesses everyone who calls on him.
Scripture says, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
But how can they call on someone they haven’t believed in? How can they believe in someone they’ve never heard of? How can they hear about him unless someone preaches to them?
And how can anyone preach to them without being sent? It is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
But not all the people of Israel accepted the good news. Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
So faith comes from hearing the message, and the message is heard through the preaching about Christ.
But I ask, “Didn’t the people of Israel hear?” Of course they did. It is written, “Their voice has gone out into the whole earth, their words from one end of the world to the other.”
Again I ask, “Didn’t Israel understand?” First, Moses says, “I will use people who aren’t a nation to make you jealous. I’ll use a nation that has no understanding to make you angry.”
And in Isaiah, God says boldly, “I was found by those who weren’t trying to find me. I made myself known to those who weren’t asking for me.”
But concerning Israel he says, “All day long I have held out my hands to a stubborn people who don’t obey me.”

verses.heading: The Israelites Who Are Faithful / The Israelites Who Are Faithful
verses.text: But let me ask, did God reject his people? Not at all! I myself belong to Israel. I am one of Abraham’s children, from the tribe of Benjamin.
God didn’t reject his people, the ones he knew ahead of time. Don’t you know what Scripture says in the story of Elijah? Elijah complained to God about Israel and said,
“Lord, they’ve killed your prophets and torn down your altars. I’m the only one left, and they’re trying to kill me.”
How did God answer him? God said, “I’ve kept 7,000 people for myself who haven’t bowed down to Baal.”
Some Israelites are also faithful today. They’ve been chosen by God’s grace.
And if they are chosen by grace, then it’s not based on anything they’ve done. If it were, then grace wouldn’t be grace anymore.
What should we say then? The people of Israel didn’t receive what they wanted so badly. Those Israelites who were chosen did receive it, but the rest of the people were made stubborn.
It is written, “God made it hard for them to understand. He gave them eyes that couldn’t see and ears that couldn’t hear, and they’re still like that today.”
David says, “Let their feast be a trap and a snare, something to make them trip and fall. Let them get what’s coming to them.
Let their eyes grow dark so they can’t see, and let their backs be bent forever.”

verses.heading: Two Kinds of Olive Branches / Two Kinds of Olive Branches
verses.text: So let me ask something else: The Israelites didn’t trip and fall so badly that they could never get up, did they? Not at all! Rather, because Israel went wrong, the Gentiles are being saved, and that should make Israel jealous of them.
But if Israel’s going wrong has brought riches to the world, and their loss has brought riches to the Gentiles, how much greater riches will come when all Israel turns back to God!
Let me talk now to you who are Gentiles. As the apostle to the Gentiles, I take pride in the work I do.
I hope that somehow I can stir up my own people to want what you have. That way maybe some of them will be saved.
When they were not accepted, it became possible for the whole world to be brought back to God. So what will happen when they are accepted? It will be like life from the dead.
When the first handful of dough is offered to God, this shows that all of the dough belongs to him. If the root of a tree belongs to God, then so do the branches that grow from it.

Some of the natural branches have been broken off. You Gentiles are like a wild olive branch that has been grafted onto the tree with the other branches. Now you’re enjoying the life-giving sap of the olive tree root.
But don’t think you’re better than the other branches. Remember, you don’t give life to the root, the root gives life to you.
You might say, “Some branches were broken off so that I could be grafted onto the tree.”
That’s true. But they were broken off because they didn’t believe. You stand only because you do believe. So don’t be proud; be careful.
If God didn’t spare the natural branches, he won’t spare you either.

Think about how kind God is! But also think about how strict he is! He was strict with those who stopped following him, but he has been kind to you. So you must continue to live in his kindness. If you don’t, you too will be cut off.
If the people of Israel don’t continue in their unbelief, they will be grafted back onto the tree. God is able to do that.

After all, weren’t you cut from a wild olive tree and grafted onto an olive tree that was being cultivated in an orchard? You didn’t come from the same kind of tree. How much more easily will the natural branches be grafted back onto their own olive tree!

verses.heading: All Israel Will Be Saved / All Israel Will Be Saved
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, here’s a mystery I want you to understand. It will keep you from being proud. Part of Israel has refused to obey God, and that will continue until the full number of Gentiles has entered God’s kingdom.
In this way all Israel will be saved. It is written, “The God who saves will come from Mount Zion. He will remove sin from Jacob’s family.
Here is my covenant with them: I will take away their sins.”

As far as the good news is concerned, the people of Israel are enemies, and this has been for your benefit. But as far as God’s choice is concerned, the people of Israel are loved because of God’s promises to the founders of their nation.
God doesn’t take back his gifts or change his mind about those he has chosen.
At one time you weren’t obeying God, but now you have received mercy because Israel didn’t obey.
In the same way, Israel hasn’t been obeying God, but now they can receive mercy because of God’s mercy to you.
God has found everyone guilty of not obeying him so that he can have mercy on everyone.

verses.heading: Praise to God / Praise to God
verses.text: God’s wisdom and knowledge are so profoundly rich! We can’t understand how he reaches such wise decisions! We can’t figure out how he deals with people so well!
“Who has known what God thinks? Or who has ever given him advice?”
“Has anyone ever given anything to God, so that God has to pay them back?”
Everything is from him and through him and for him. May God be given the glory forever! Amen.

verses.heading: Living as a Holy Sacrifice to God / Living as a Holy Sacrifice to God
verses.text: Because God has shown you such mercy, brothers and sisters, I ask you to offer up your bodies to God while you are still alive. That will be a sacrifice that is holy and pleasing to God. It’s the right kind of worship to offer God.

Don’t live the way this world lives. Let your way of thinking be completely changed. Then you’ll be able to recognize what God wants for you and agree that what he wants is right. His plan is good and pleasing and perfect.

verses.heading: Serving One Another in the Body of Christ / Serving One Another in the Body of Christ
verses.text: By the grace that has been given to me, I say to every one of you, don’t think of yourself more highly than you should. Have a reasonable view of yourself, based on the faith God has given to each of you.
Each of us has one body that’s made up of many parts. Those parts don’t all have the same function.
In the same way, we are all part of one body in Christ, even though there are many of us. And each part of the body belongs to all the other parts.
We all have different gifts, according to the grace God has given to each of us. If you have the gift of prophecy, then use it according to the faith you have.
If your gift is serving, then serve. If it’s teaching, then teach.
If it’s encouraging others, then encourage them. If it’s giving, then give generously. If it’s being a leader, then do it diligently. If it’s showing mercy, then do it cheerfully.

verses.heading: Love in Action / Love in Action
verses.text: Love must be sincere. Hate what is evil. Hold on to what is good.
Love one another deeply. Honor one another more than yourselves.
Don’t ever become complacent, but stay excited about your faith as you serve the Lord.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and faithful in prayer.
Share with the Lord’s people who are in need. Welcome one another into your homes.
Bless those who keep hurting you. Bless them, don’t curse them.
If someone is happy, share their happiness, and if someone is sad, share their sadness.
Get along with one another. Don’t be proud, but be willing to befriend people who aren’t considered important. Don’t think you’re better than others.
Don’t pay back evil with evil. Be careful to do what everyone considers right.
If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.

My dear friends, don’t try to get even with other people. Leave it up to God to punish them. After all, it’s written that the Lord says, “I’m the one who punishes people who do wrong, and I will pay them back.”
On the contrary, “If your enemies are hungry, give them food to eat. If they’re thirsty, give them something to drink. If you do that, you will pile up burning coals on their heads.”
Don’t be overcome by evil. Overcome evil by doing good.

verses.heading: Obey Those in Authority / Obey Those in Authority
verses.text: Everyone should obey the government, because the government gets its authority from God. God has established the government.
So whoever rebels against the government is rebelling against an authority that God has established, and anyone who does that will be judged.

If you do what’s right, you won’t need to be afraid of your rulers. But if you do what’s wrong, watch out! You don’t want to be afraid of those in authority, do you? Then do what’s right, and you’ll be praised.

The one in authority serves God for your good. But if you do wrong, watch out! Rulers have been given the power of punishment for a good reason. They’re working for God, and it’s on God’s behalf that they punish people who do wrong.
So you must obey the authorities, and not just so that you won’t be punished, but because that’s the right thing to do.
You must also pay taxes for the same reason. The authorities are working full time for God as rulers, and they need to be supported.

Give everyone what you owe them. If you owe taxes, then pay them. If you owe other fees, then pay those. And don’t forget that you also owe your leaders respect and honor and that you should give them those things.

verses.heading: Love Fulfills the Law / Love Fulfills the Law
verses.text: Pay all your debts back on time. But you can never pay back all the love you owe one another. Whoever loves other people has done everything the law requires.

There’s a commandment that says, “Love your neighbor as you love yourself.” That one command sums up all the others, including “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not commit murder,” “Do not steal,” and, “Don’t want what belongs to others.”
Love never does anything wrong to a neighbor. Instead, love does all the good things the law requires.

verses.heading: The Day Is Near / The Day Is Near
verses.text: When you do these things, keep in mind the times we’re living in. The time has already come for you to wake up from your sleep. The full effects of our salvation are closer now than when we first believed in Christ.
The night is nearly over and the day is almost here. So let’s put off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Let’s act properly, like people living in the daytime. Don’t go to wild parties and don’t get drunk. Don’t do anything immoral or indecent. Don’t get into fights or be jealous of anyone.
Instead, develop the qualities of the Lord Jesus Christ in your life, and don’t think about how to satisfy any wrong desires.

verses.heading: The Weak and the Strong / The Weak and the Strong
verses.text: If someone’s faith is weak, welcome them, but not so that you can argue with them about differences of opinion.
One person’s faith allows them to eat anything, but another person whose faith is weak doesn’t eat any meat, in case some of it has been offered to idols.
A person who eats everything must not look down someone who doesn’t. A person who doesn’t eat everything must not judge someone who does. God has accepted them.
Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? Whether they’re faithful or not is their own master’s concern. And they will be faithful, because the Lord is able to make them faithful.
One person considers one day to be better than the rest, while another person considers every day to be just as good. Each person should be fully convinced in their own mind.

Whoever treats one day as different from the rest does that to honor the Lord. Whoever eats meat does that to honor the Lord, and they give thanks to God, while whoever doesn’t eat meat does that to honor the Lord, and they too give thanks to God.
We don’t live for ourselves only, and we don’t die for ourselves only.
If we live, we live to honor the Lord, and if we die, we die to honor the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
Christ died and came back to life in order to become the Lord of both the dead and the living.
So then, who are you to judge your brother or sister? Why do you act as if you’re better than they are? We will all stand before God as our judge.
It is written, “ ‘As surely as I’m alive,’ says the Lord, ‘everyone will kneel down in front of me, and everyone will admit that I’m God.’ ”
So we will all have to answer to God for the things we’ve done.
Let’s not judge each other anymore. Instead, let’s decide not to put anything in a brother or sister’s way that would make them trip and fall.
I’m convinced, because the Lord Jesus has convinced me of this, that nothing is unclean in itself. But someone may consider a thing to be unclean. If they do, it is unclean for them.
If what you eat makes your brother or sister upset, then you’re no longer acting in love. Don’t let what you eat destroy someone Christ died for.
Don’t let something you know is good be spoken of as if it were evil.
The kingdom of God isn’t about eating or drinking. It’s about doing what’s right and having peace and joy through the Holy Spirit.
Those who serve Christ in this way are pleasing to God, and people approve of them too.
So let’s do all we can to live in peace, and let’s work hard to build one another up.
Don’t destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean. But it’s wrong to eat anything that might cause someone else to trip and fall.
It’s better not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything else that would cause your brother or sister to fall.
Whatever you believe about these things, keep between yourself and God. Blessed is the person who doesn’t feel guilty for what they do.

But whoever has doubts about something they might eat is guilty if they do eat it. That’s because they don’t believe that they should be eating it, and if you do something even though you don’t believe you should, that’s sin.
We who are strong should accommodate those who are weak and not please only ourselves.
Each of us should please our neighbors for their good in order to build them up.
Even Christ did not please himself. It is written, “The bad things people have said about you have also been aimed at me.”
Everything written in the past was written to teach us, so that we would have hope both through the endurance the Scriptures teach and through the encouragement they provide.
May the God who gives endurance and encouragement give you the same attitude toward one another that Christ Jesus had.
Then with one mind and voice you will give glory to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Christ has accepted you, so accept one another in order to bring praise to God.
I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the Jews on behalf of God’s truth, so that the promises made to the founders of our nation would be confirmed.
He also did this so that the Gentiles would give glory to God for his mercy. It is written, “I will praise you among the Gentiles. I will sing the praises of your name.”
Again it says, “You Gentiles, rejoice together with God’s people.”
And again it says, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles; let all the nations sing praises to him.”
And Isaiah says, “The Root of Jesse will grow up quickly. He will rule over the nations, and the Gentiles will put their hope in him.”
May the God who gives hope fill you with great joy and peace as you trust in him, and may you overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

verses.heading: Paul Serves the Gentiles / Paul Serves the Gentiles
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, I’m sure that you are full of goodness, filled with knowledge, and able to teach one another.
But I’ve written to you very boldly about some things to remind you of them again, because of the grace God gave me
to serve Christ Jesus among the Gentiles. I’m like a priest of the good news, and I want the Gentiles to be an offering that pleases God because it has been made holy by the Holy Spirit.
Thanks to Christ Jesus, I can take pride in the work I’ve done for God.
I don’t dare to speak about anything except what Christ has done through me. He has been leading the Gentiles to obey God through what I have said and done,
through the power of signs and wonders, and through the power of the Spirit of God. I have now preached the good news about Christ to everyone from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.
I’ve always wanted to preach the good news where Christ is not known. I don’t want to build on someone else’s foundation.
Instead, as it is written, “Those who were not told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
That’s why I have often been kept from coming to you.

verses.heading: Paul Plans to Visit Rome / Paul Plans to Visit Rome
verses.text: But now that there isn’t anywhere else for me to work in these areas, and since I’ve been wanting to visit you for many years,
I plan to see you when I go to Spain. I hope to visit you on my way there, and I hope you’ll help me get the rest of the way once we’ve had a good visit together.
But right now I’m heading to Jerusalem to serve the Lord’s people there.
The believers in Macedonia and Achaia have kindly taken an offering to help the poor among the Lord’s people in Jerusalem.

They were glad to do it, and it acknowledges their debt of gratitude. After all, if the Gentiles have shared in the Jews’ spiritual blessings, they should also share their own earthly blessings with the Jews.
So first I’m going to finish this task and make sure that the poor in Jerusalem receive this offering, and then I’ll go to Spain and visit you on my way.
I know that when I come, I’ll be bringing the full blessing of Christ to you.
I ask you, brothers and sisters, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Holy Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.
Pray that I’ll be kept safe from those in Judea who do not believe. And pray that the offering I’m taking to Jerusalem will be well received by the Lord’s people there.
That way, I’ll be full of joy when come to you, if that’s God’s will, and we’ll have a refreshing time together.
May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

verses.heading: Personal Greetings / Personal Greetings
verses.text: Let me introduce our sister Phoebe, who’s bringing this letter to you as my representative. She’s a deacon of the church in Cenchreae.

Please offer her your hospitality, in the way God’s people should welcome a fellow believer. I ask you to help with anything she might need from you, because she has been very helpful to many people herself, including me.
Greet Priscilla and Aquila, who work together with me in serving Christ Jesus.
They have put their lives in danger for me, and I’m thankful for them, as are all the Gentile churches.
Also please greet the church that meets in their house. Greet my dear friend Epenetus. He was the first person in the province of Asia to believe in Christ.
Greet Mary, who worked very hard for you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow Jews. They have been in prison with me, and they are leaders among the apostles. They became believers in Christ before I did.
Greet Ampliatus, my dear friend in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, who works together with me in serving Christ, and greet my dear friend Stachys.
Greet Apelles, who remained faithful to Christ even when he was tested. Greet those who live in the house of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my fellow Jew. Greet the believers who live in the house of Narcissus.
Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, those women who work hard for the Lord. Greet my dear friend Persis, another woman who has worked very hard for the Lord.
Greet Rufus, a chosen believer in the Lord, and greet his mother, who has been a mother to me too.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the other brothers and sisters with them.
Greet Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas, and all of the Lord’s people who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send their greetings.
I warn you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who cause divisions and who trip you up by teaching you things that are the opposite of what you’ve learned. Stay away from them,
because people like that are serving their own appetites, not our Lord Jesus Christ. With smooth talk and flattery they fool people who don’t know any better.
But everyone has heard that you obey God, and that makes me very happy. I want you to be wise about what is good but not know anything about what is evil.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. May the grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
Timothy, who works with me, sends you his greetings. So do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow Jews.
I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter as Paul dictated it, greet you in the Lord.

Gaius sends you his greetings. I’m staying with him here, and the whole church meets in his house. Erastus, the director of public works here in the city, and our brother Quartus send you their greetings.
God is able to strengthen you through the good news, which is the message I preach about Jesus Christ. There was a mystery that had been kept hidden for a very long time.

But now it has been made known to all the Gentiles through the writings of the prophets, as the eternal God has commanded. Through the revelation of this mystery, the Gentiles are starting to obey God by trusting in him.
May the only wise God receive glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
From Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes.

To the members of God’s church in Corinth. You have been made holy in Christ Jesus, and you’ve been called to be his holy people together with all those everywhere who pray to our Lord Jesus Christ, who is their Lord and ours.
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.

verses.heading: Paul Gives Thanks / Paul Gives Thanks
verses.text: I always thank my God for you because of the grace he has given you in Christ Jesus.
Through him God has enriched you in every way, in speech and in knowledge,
so you’ve been able to recognize that what we told you about Christ is true.
You have every gift of the Holy Spirit as you wait eagerly for our Lord Jesus Christ to return.
God will keep you strong to the very end, so that you will be blameless on the day he returns.
God is faithful, and he has called you into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.heading: The Report About Arguments / The Report About Arguments
verses.text: I ask all of you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to agree with one another and not argue. Look and think about things in the same way.
My brothers and sisters, I say this because some people from Chloe’s family have told me that you’re arguing with one another.
Here’s what I mean. One of you says, “I follow Paul.” Another says, “I follow Apollos.” Another says, “I follow Peter.” And still another says, “I follow Christ.”
Is Christ divided? Did Paul die on the cross for you? Were you baptized in the name of Paul?
I thank God that I didn’t baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so that no one can say they were baptized in my name.
(Oh, right, I also baptized Stephanas and those in his house. I don’t remember if I baptized anyone else.)

Christ didn’t send me to baptize; he sent me to preach the good news. But I wasn’t supposed to try to persuade you with fancy words, because that would take all the power away from the cross of Christ.

verses.heading: Christ Is God’s Power and Wisdom
verses.subheading: Christ Is God’s Power and Wisdom
verses.text: The message of the cross seems foolish to those who are lost. But to us who are being saved, it is the power of God.
It is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of those who are wise. I will do away with the cleverness of those who think they’re so smart.”
Where is the wise person? Where is the teacher of the law? Where are the great thinkers of our time? Hasn’t God made the wisdom of the world foolish?
God wisely planned that the world wouldn’t be able to understand him through its own wisdom. Instead, God was happy to use the foolish things we preach to save those who believe.
Jews want to see signs and Greeks look for wisdom,
but we preach about Christ and his death on the cross. That’s very hard for Jews to accept, and Gentiles think it’s foolish.
But to everyone God has called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is God’s power and God’s wisdom.
The foolish things of God are wiser than human wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.

Brothers and sisters, think of what you were when God called you. Not many of you were considered wise by human standards. Not many of you were influential. Not many of you came from important families.
But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise. God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
God chose the things of this world that are common, and which are looked down on as if they were nothing, in order to discredit the things that are considered significant.
That way no one can brag to God about who or what they are.
Because of what God has done, you belong to Christ Jesus. He has become God’s wisdom for us. He makes us right with God, he makes us holy, and he sets us free.
It is written, “The one who boasts should boast about what the Lord has done.”
And that’s how it was with me, brothers and sisters. When I came to you, I didn’t use fancy words or human wisdom to preach the truth to you about God’s love.
My goal while I was with you was to talk about only one thing: Jesus Christ and his death on the cross.
When I came to you, I was weak and afraid and shaking all over.
I didn’t preach my message with clever and compelling words. Instead, my preaching showed the Holy Spirit’s power.
This was so that your faith would be based on God’s power and not on human wisdom.

verses.heading: God’s Wisdom Through the Holy Spirit
verses.subheading: God’s Wisdom Through the Holy Spirit
verses.text: However, when we speak to those who are mature in the faith, we do share our wisdom. But it’s not the wisdom of this world or its rulers, who are fading away.
No, we share God’s wisdom, which is a mystery that has been hidden until now. But before time began, God planned that this wisdom would bring us heavenly glory.
None of the rulers of this world understood God’s wisdom. If they had, they wouldn’t have nailed the Lord of glory to the cross.
It is written that “no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human mind has imagined” the things God has prepared for those who love him.
But God has shown these things to us through his Spirit. The Spirit understands all things, even the deep things of God.
Who can know the thoughts of another person? Only that person’s own spirit. In the same way, only the Spirit of God knows God’s thoughts.
What we have received is not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we can understand what God has freely given us.
That’s what we speak about, and we don’t use words that we’ve learned from human wisdom. We use words that the Holy Spirit has taught us, and we use them to explain spiritual truths.

The person who doesn’t have the Spirit doesn’t accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. Those things seem foolish to them, and they can’t understand them, because they can’t be understood without the Spirit’s help.
But the person who does have the Spirit can make judgments about everything, though no human being can judge them. It is written,
“Who can ever know the Lord’s mind? Can anyone teach him anything?” But we have the mind of Christ.

verses.heading: The Church and Its Leaders
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I couldn’t speak to you as people who were led by the Holy Spirit. I had to speak to you as people who were still following their own wrong desires. You’re not growing as Christ wants you to. You’re still like babies.
The words I spoke to you were like milk, not solid food. You weren’t ready for solid food, and you’re still not ready for it.
You’re still following your own wrong desires. If you’re jealous and you’re arguing, aren’t those desires in charge? Aren’t you acting like ordinary human beings?
When one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another says, “I follow Apollos,” aren’t you acting like ordinary human beings?
After all, what is Apollos? And what is Paul? Only servants who helped you to believe. The Lord has given each of us our own work to do.
I planted the seed, and Apollos watered it, but God has been making it grow.
So the one who plants doesn’t matter, and neither does the one who waters. It’s God who matters. He makes things grow.
The one who plants and the one who waters have the same goal, and the Lord will give each of them a reward for their work.
We’re working together to serve God. You’re like God’s field and God’s building.
God has given me the grace to lay a foundation as a wise builder. Now someone else is building on it. But each one should build carefully.
No one can lay any other foundation than the one that has already been laid, and that foundation is Jesus Christ.
A person might build on it using gold, silver, jewels, wood, hay, or straw.
Every person’s work will be recognized for what it is, because the Day of Judgment will expose it. Everyone’s work will be put through fire to test how good it is.
If what a person has built doesn’t burn up, God will give them a reward for their work.
If what a person has built does burn up, they’ll lose everything. They’ll still be saved, but only like someone escaping from a fire.
Don’t you know that together you are God’s temple? Don’t you know that God’s Spirit lives among you?
If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person. God’s temple is holy, and you together are that temple.
Don’t fool yourselves. If any of you think you’re wise by the standards of the world, you should become “fools” so that you can become truly wise.
The wisdom of this world is foolish in God’s eyes. It is written, “God catches wise people in their own clever plans.”
It is also written, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of wise people don’t really amount to anything.”
So don’t brag any more about human leaders! Everything is yours,
including Paul and Apollos and Peter, and the world and life and death and the present and the future. All these things are yours,
and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.

verses.heading: True Apostles of Christ
verses.text: So here’s how you should think of us. We’re servants of Christ who’ve been trusted with the mysteries God has shown us.
Those who’ve been trusted with something must show that they’re dependable.
I really don’t care if you judge me, or if any human court judges me. I don’t even judge myself.
I don’t feel I have done anything wrong, but that doesn’t mean I’m not guilty. It’s the Lord who judges me.

So don’t judge anything before the appointed time. Wait until the Lord returns, and he will bring what’s now hidden in the dark out into the light. He’ll show the real reasons why people do what they do. At that time God will give each person the praise they deserve.

Brothers and sisters, I’ve used myself and Apollos as examples. I want to help you learn from us what the saying means, “Don’t go beyond what’s written.” If you understand that, you won’t feel proud that you follow one of us instead of the other.
Who thinks you’re different from anyone else? What do you have that wasn’t given to you? And if it was given to you, why do you brag as though it came from you?

You think you already have everything you need. You think you’ve already become rich and that you’ve begun to rule, even though we haven’t. I wish that you really had begun to rule. Then we’d be ruling with you!

It feels as if God has put us apostles on display like the people who are put at the end of the procession to the arena because they’re going to die there. And it feels as if the whole universe is watching, both angels and humans.
We’re fools for Christ, but you’re so wise in Christ! We’re weak, but you’re so strong! You are honored, but we’re looked down on!
We’re still hungry and thirsty, dressed in rags, homeless, and treated badly.
We work hard with our own hands. When others curse us, we bless them. When we’re attacked, we don’t fight back.
When others say bad things about us, we answer with kind words. We’ve become the world’s garbage, and we’re still everybody’s trash even now.

verses.heading: Paul Warns Against Pride
verses.text: I’m not writing this to make you ashamed, but to warn you as my dear children.
Other people might be your guardians in Christ, but even if there were 10,000 of them, you still wouldn’t have many fathers. I became your father in Christ Jesus by telling you the good news.
So I’m asking you to follow my example.

That’s the reason why I’ve sent Timothy to you. He’s like a son to me, and I love him. He’s faithful in serving the Lord. He’ll remind you of the way I live as a servant of Christ Jesus. I myself follow what I teach everywhere in all the churches.
Some of you have become proud. You act as if I weren’t coming to you.
But I am going to come very soon, if that’s the Lord’s will. Then I’ll find out if there’s actually any power behind what these proud people are saying.
The kingdom of God isn’t a matter of talk but a matter of power.
Which would you prefer? Do you want me to come and punish you? Or do you want me to come in love, with a gentle spirit?

verses.heading: The Report About a Sinful Man / The Report About a Sinful Man
verses.text: It’s actually reported that there is a sexual sin among you that’s so bad even people who don’t know God wouldn’t tolerate it. I’m told that a man is sleeping with his father’s wife.
And you’re proud of this! Shouldn’t you be grieving instead? Shouldn’t you have thrown this man out from among you?
Even though I’m not there with you physically, I am with you in spirit. And because I’m with you in spirit, in the name of our Lord Jesus I’ve already judged the man who’s doing this.
So when you gather together, and I’m with you in spirit, and the power of our Lord Jesus is also present,
hand this man over to Satan. His body may be destroyed, but his spirit will be saved on the day the Lord returns.
Your bragging isn’t good. Don’t you know that just a little yeast makes the whole batch of dough rise?
Get rid of the old yeast. Then you can be like a new batch of dough without yeast. That’s what you really are already, because Christ, our Passover Lamb, has been sacrificed for us.
So let’s celebrate the Feast, but not with the old bread made with the yeast of hatred and wrongdoing. Let’s celebrate it with bread made without yeast, the bread of honesty and truth.
I told you in my previous letter that you should stay away from people who commit sexual sins.

I didn’t mean the people of this world who sin that way. And I wasn’t saying you should stay away from all people who are greedy, or who cheat others, or who worship statues of gods. To do that, you’d have to leave the world entirely!

So let me clarify in this letter what I meant: You should stay away from anyone who claims to be a believer but who commits sexual sins, or is greedy, or worships idols, or tells lies about others, or gets drunk, or cheats. Don’t even eat with people like that.
What business do I have judging those who are outside the church? But aren’t you supposed to judge those who are inside the church?
God will judge those outside. But as for those inside, as Scripture says, “Throw out that person who’s doing wrong!”

verses.heading: The Report About Lawsuits / The Report About Lawsuits
verses.text: When one of you is in a dispute with another believer, how dare you take them to court to be judged by ungodly people! Why don’t you ask the Lord’s people to help you settle it?
Don’t you know that the Lord’s people will judge the world? Since you’re going to do that, don’t you think you can judge small cases?
Don’t you know that we’re even going to judge angels? We should certainly be able to judge the things of this life!
So if you’re in a dispute with someone, should you ask people that the church doesn’t even respect to settle it? Of course not!
You should be ashamed. Is it possible that none of you are wise enough to settle disputes between believers,
so that they’re taking each other to court instead, in front of unbelievers?
Just by getting into a lawsuit with another believer, you’ve already lost. Wouldn’t it be better to be treated wrongly instead? Wouldn’t it be better just to be cheated?
Instead, you’re cheating and doing wrong yourselves, and you’re doing it to your own brothers and sisters.
Don’t you know that people who do wrong won’t inherit God’s kingdom? Don’t be deceived. People who commit sexual sins, or who worship idols or commit adultery, or men who sleep with other men,
or thieves or greedy people, or those who are often drunk or tell lies or cheat, will not inherit God’s kingdom.
Some of you used to do things like that. But you were washed and made holy and right with God in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.

verses.heading: The Report About Sexual Sins / The Report About Sexual Sins
verses.text: Some of you are saying, “I have the right to do anything.” That may be true, but not everything is helpful. If you say, “I have the right to do anything,” you should also say, “But I won’t be controlled by anything.”

Some of you are saying, “Food is meant for the stomach, and the stomach is meant for food, and God will destroy both of them.” But you can’t say the same thing about the body and sexual sins. The body is meant for the Lord, and the Lord is meant for the body.
By his power God raised the Lord from the dead, and he will raise us up too.
Don’t you know that your bodies are part of Christ himself? Should I take a part of Christ and join it to a prostitute? Never!
Don’t you know that when you have sex with a prostitute, you become one with her in body? Scripture says, “The two will become one.”
But whoever is joined to the Lord becomes one with him in spirit.
So keep far away from sexual sins. All the other sins a person commits are outside the body. But if a person commits sexual sins, those are sins against their own body.
Don’t you know that together you are a body, which is the temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you? You have received the Spirit from God. You don’t belong to yourselves;
you were bought with a price. So honor God together as one body.

verses.heading: The Question About Marriage / The Question About Marriage
verses.text: Now let me address the things you wrote to me about. Some of you are saying, “It’s good for a man not to sleep with a woman,” as if that were more spiritual.
But since you can’t control yourselves, this is leading to sexual sin. So each man should sleep with his own wife and each woman should sleep with her own husband.
A husband should satisfy his wife’s needs, and a wife should satisfy her husband’s needs.
The wife’s body doesn’t belong only to her; it also belongs to her husband. In the same way, the husband’s body doesn’t belong only to him; it also belongs to his wife.

Don’t deprive each other. You could agree not to have sexual relations for a while if you really needed time to pray. But after that, you should go back to having sexual relations. Otherwise, Satan will tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
(I’m giving you permission to do this; I’m not telling you that you should.)
I wish all of you were single like me. But each person has their own gift from God. One has the gift of being happily married, and another has the gift of being happily single.
I think it would be good if those of you who aren’t married or who are widowed could stay single like me.
But if you couldn’t control yourselves, then you should get married. It’s better to get married than to burn with desire.
But as for those who are married, I need to give you a command that comes directly from the Lord Jesus, not from me: A wife must not leave her husband.
If she does, she must stay unmarried or else go back to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.

I know that some of the rest of you are in a complicated situation. We don’t have a direct command from the Lord about that, but let me offer some advice. If a brother has a wife who isn’t a believer, he shouldn’t divorce her if she’s willing to live with him.
In the same way, if a woman has a husband who isn’t a believer, she shouldn’t divorce him if he’s willing to live with her.

An unbelieving husband is made holy through his wife, and an unbelieving wife is made holy through her believing husband. If that weren’t true, your children wouldn’t be clean. But since it is true, they are holy.
But if the unbeliever wants to leave, let them go. In that case, the believer isn’t bound to them. God wants us to live in peace.
Wife, how do you know whether you will save your husband? Husband, how do you know whether you will save your wife?

verses.heading: Stay as You Were When God Chose You
verses.subheading: Stay as You Were When God Chose You
verses.text: But each person should live as a believer in whatever situation the Lord has assigned to them. Stay as you were when God chose you. That’s the rule I tell people to follow in all the churches.
If a man was already circumcised when he was called, then he shouldn’t become uncircumcised. If he was uncircumcised when he was called, then he shouldn’t be circumcised.
Being circumcised means nothing and being uncircumcised means nothing. Doing what God commands is what matters.
Each of you should stay as you were when God chose you.
Were you a slave when God called you? Don’t let that trouble you, although if you can gain your freedom, you should do that.
Someone who was a slave when the Lord called them is now serving the Lord as a free person. But it’s just as true that someone who was free when God called them is now a slave of Christ.
You were bought with a price, so don’t become slaves of human beings.
Brothers and sisters, each person should stay as they were when God called them, knowing that God will be with them in that situation.

verses.heading: Advice for Those Who Are Engaged
verses.subheading: Advice for Those Who Are Engaged
verses.text: Now let me speak to those who are engaged. I don’t have a direct command from the Lord for you. But I’d like to give my opinion as someone who, by the Lord’s mercy, can be trusted.
Times are difficult right now, so I think it’s good for a man to stay as he is.
Are you engaged to a woman? Then don’t break the engagement. Are you not engaged to anyone? Then don’t look for a wife.
But if you do marry someone, you haven’t sinned. And if a woman marries her fiancé, she hasn’t sinned. But those who do marry will have many troubles in this life, and I want to spare you from those.
What I mean, brothers and sisters, is that the time is short. From now on, those who have a husband or wife should live as if they didn’t have one.
Those who are mourning should live as if they weren’t, and those who are rejoicing should live as if they weren’t. Those who buy something should live as if it weren’t theirs to keep,
and those who use the things of this world shouldn’t become all wrapped up in them. The world as it now exists is passing away.
I don’t want you to have anything to worry about. A single man is concerned about the things of the Lord. He wants to know how he can please the Lord.
But a married man is concerned about the things of this world. He wants to know how he can please his wife.

So he’s pulled in two directions. An unmarried or single woman is concerned about the things of the Lord. She wants to be devoted to the Lord in both body and spirit. But a married woman is concerned about the things of this world. She wants to know how she can please her husband.
I’m saying these things for your own good. I’m not trying to hold you back. I want you to be free to live in a right way and devote yourselves completely to the Lord.

Suppose someone is worried that he’s not acting honorably toward his fiancée. Suppose his desires are too strong, and he feels that he should marry her. He should do as he wants. That wouldn’t be a sin. They should get married.

But suppose a man has made up his mind not to marry his fiancée. He has no compelling need to get married; he’s able to control himself. If that’s what he has decided, then he’s also doing the right thing.
So then, the man who marries his fiancée is doing the right thing, but the man who doesn’t marry his fiancée is doing an even better thing.
A woman has to stay married to her husband for as long as he lives. If he dies, she’s free to marry anyone she wants. But the man she marries must belong to the Lord.
In my opinion, she’s happier if she stays single. I say that as someone who has the Spirit of God too.

verses.heading: The Question About Food Sacrificed to Idols / The Question About Food Sacrificed to Idols
verses.text: Now I’d like to talk about food that has been sacrificed to statues of gods. We know that “We all have knowledge.” But knowledge makes people proud, while love builds them up.
Those who think they know something still don’t know as they should.
But whoever loves God is known by God.
So then, here’s what I say about eating food sacrificed to idols. We know that “an idol really is nothing at all in the world.” We know that “there is only one God.”
There may be so-called gods either in heaven or on earth. In fact, there are many “gods” and many “lords.”
But for us there is only one God, the Father. All things came from him, and we live for him. And there is only one Lord, Jesus Christ. All things came through him and we live through him.

But not everyone knows this. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that when they eat sacrificial food, they think of it as having been sacrificed to real gods. And because their conscience is weak, they feel guilty.
Eating sacrificial food doesn’t prove how close to God we are. We aren’t any worse off if we don’t eat it, and we aren’t any better off if we do.
So be careful how you use your rights. Make sure you don’t cause someone who’s weaker than you to fall into sin.

Suppose that you, with all of your knowledge, are eating in a temple of one of those gods. And suppose someone whose conscience is weak sees you. Won’t that person think it’s okay to eat food sacrificed to honor “gods” and be encouraged to do so?
If that happens, then your knowledge will destroy that weaker brother or sister Christ died for.
If you sin against them that way and wound their weak conscience, you’re actually sinning against Christ.
So if eating food sacrificed to idols would cause my brother or sister to fall into sin, I’ll never eat that food again. That way, I won’t ever cause them to fall.

verses.heading: Paul’s Rights as an Apostle
verses.text: Aren’t I free? Aren’t I an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus our Lord? Aren’t you the result of my work for the Lord?
Others might not think of me as an apostle, but I’m certainly one to you! You’re the proof that I am the Lord’s apostle.
This is how I defend myself when people judge me.
Don’t we have the right to eat and drink?
Don’t we have the right to take a believing wife along with us when we travel? That’s what the other apostles do, and the Lord’s brothers and Peter do the same.
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who have to do other work to support ourselves while we serve as apostles?

Who serves as a soldier but has to pay his own expenses? Who plants a vineyard but doesn’t get to eat any of its grapes? Who takes care of a flock but doesn’t get to drink any of the milk from the sheep?
Do I say this only on human authority? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?
It’s written in the Law of Moses, “Don’t stop an ox from eating while it helps separate the grain from the straw.” But is God concerned only for oxen?
Isn’t he saying that for all of us too? Yes, it was written for us. Whoever plows and whoever separates the grain has a right to hope that they will share in the harvest.
We have planted spiritual seed among you. Is it too much for us to expect to receive some material things from you?

If others have the right to receive support from you, don’t we have an even greater right? But we haven’t used that right. No, we’re prepared to make any sacrifice we have to, rather than let anything get in the way of the good news of Christ.
Don’t you know that people who serve in the temple get their food from the temple, and that people who serve at the altar eat the food that’s offered on the altar?
So those who preach the good news should also receive their living from that work. That’s what the Lord has commanded.

But I haven’t used any of those rights. And I’m not writing this because I want you to do things like that for me. I’d rather die than let anyone take away the satisfaction I get from bragging about this.
I’m not bragging about preaching the good news. I have to preach the good news—woe to me if I don’t!
If I preach because I want to, I get a reward. If I preach because I have to, I’m only doing my duty.
So what reward do I get? Here’s my reward: being able to offer the good news free of charge, without claiming all my rights as a person who preaches the good news.

verses.heading: Paul Uses His Freedom to Share the Good News
verses.subheading: Paul Uses His Freedom to Share the Good News
verses.text: I’m free and I don’t belong to anyone, but I’ve made myself a slave to everyone. I’ve done that to win as many people as I can to Christ.

To the Jews I became like a Jew, in order to win the Jews. To those who are under the law, I became like one who was under the law, even though I’m actually not under the law myself, in order to win those under the law.
To those who don’t have the law, I became like one who didn’t have the law (even though I’m not free from God’s law, but under Christ’s law), in order to win those who don’t have the law.
To those who are weak I became weak, in order to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
I do all of this for the sake of the good news, so that I can share in its blessings.

verses.heading: Training to Win the Prize
verses.text: Don’t you know that in a race, all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? So run in a way that will get you the prize.
Everyone who competes in the games trains hard. They do that to get a crown that won’t last. But we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
So I don’t run like someone who doesn’t know where the finish line is. I don’t fight like a boxer who hits nothing but air.
No, I train my body and bring it under control, so that after I’ve preached to others, I won’t be disqualified myself.

verses.heading: Warnings From Israel’s History
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I want you to know something about our people who lived long ago. They were all led by the cloud through the desert, and they all walked through the Red Sea.
They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
They all ate the same spiritual food,
and they all drank the same spiritual drink. They drank from the spiritual rock that went along with them, and that rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, and their bodies were scattered in the desert.
Now those things happened as examples for us, to keep us from wanting evil things the way they did.
So don’t worship idols, as some of them did. It is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink. Then they got up to dance wildly in front of their god.”
We shouldn’t commit sexual sins, as some of them did—and in one day, 23,000 of them died.
We shouldn’t test the Lord, as some of them did—and they were killed by snakes.
And don’t speak against God, as some of the people of Israel did—and they were killed by the destroying angel.
Those things happened to them as examples, and they were written down as a warning to us. We’re living at the time when God’s work is being completed.
So if you think you’re standing firm, be careful—you might fall.

You’re tempted in the same way that all other human beings are. And God is faithful; he won’t let you be tempted beyond what you can endure. When you are tempted, God will provide a way out, and then you’ll be able to resist.

verses.heading: Sharing in the Lord’s Supper
verses.text: My dear friends, stay far away from the worship of idols.
I know I’m talking to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.
We give thanks for the cup at the Lord’s Supper. When we do, aren’t we sharing in the blood of Christ? When we break the bread, aren’t we sharing in the body of Christ?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body, because we all share the one loaf.
Think about the people of Israel. Don’t those who eat the offerings share in the worship that takes place at the altar?
Do I mean that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
No! But the sacrifices of those who worship idols are really offered to demons, not to God, and I don’t want you to have anything to do with demons.
You can’t drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too. You can’t have a part in both the Lord’s table and the table of demons.
Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than he is?

verses.heading: The Believer’s Freedom
verses.text: You say, “I have the right to do anything,” but not everything is helpful. “I have the right to do anything,” you say, but not everything builds us up.
No one should look out only for their own interests. Instead, they should look out for the interests of others.
With a clear conscience you can eat anything that’s sold in the meat market.
Scripture says, “The earth belongs to the Lord, and so does everything in it.”
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, with a clear conscience you can eat anything that’s put in front of you.
But if someone says to you, “This food has been sacrificed to an idol,” then don’t eat it, for the sake of the person who told you and for the sake of conscience.
I’m talking about the other person’s conscience, not yours. Why should my freedom be judged by what someone else thinks?
If I’ve given thanks for my food, then I shouldn’t be blamed for eating something that I’ve thanked God for.
So whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do it all for the glory of God.
Don’t do anything that causes other people to trip and fall, whether Jews or Greeks or God’s church.
Follow my example. I try to please everyone in every way. I’m not looking out for what’s good for me. I’m looking out for the interests of others, so that they might be saved.
Follow my example, just as I follow the example of Christ.

verses.heading: The Report About Head Coverings / The Report About Head Coverings
verses.text: I commend you for remembering what I taught you and for staying true to exactly what I passed on to you.
But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head. It’s the same as having her head shaved.
If a woman doesn’t cover her head, she might as well have her hair cut off. But if it’s a disgrace for her to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, then she should cover her head.
A man shouldn’t cover his head, since he’s the likeness and glory of God. But woman is the glory of man.
Man didn’t come from woman, but woman came from man.
Also, man wasn’t created for woman, but woman was created for man.
That’s why a woman should have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
But here’s how things are for those who belong to the Lord. Woman isn’t independent of man, and man isn’t independent of woman.
Though woman first came from man, now man is born from woman. And everything comes from God.
You be the judge. Is it proper for a woman to pray to God without covering her head?
Doesn’t the very nature of things teach you that if a man has long hair, that’s disgraceful to him,
but that if a woman has long hair, that’s her glory? Long hair is given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, let me simply say that we don’t have any other practice, and none of God’s churches do either.

verses.heading: The Report About Selfishness at the Lord’s Supper / The Report About Selfishness at the Lord’s Supper
verses.text: In the following matters, I don’t commend you, because your meetings are doing more harm than good.
First, here’s what people are telling me. When you get together as a church, you split up into opposing groups. And in some ways, I believe that,
because those of you who are genuine are bound to stand out as different!
But when you come together, it’s not the Lord’s Supper that you’re eating.
As you eat, some of you go ahead and eat your own private meals. Because of this, one person doesn’t get enough to eat, while another gets drunk.

Don’t you have your own homes to eat and drink in? Or do you think so little of God’s church that you’re prepared to humiliate those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I praise you? Certainly not about this!
I passed on to you what I received from the Lord. On the night the Lord Jesus was handed over to his enemies, he took bread,
and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, given for you. Every time you eat it, do this in memory of me.”
In the same way, he took the cup after supper and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Every time you drink it, do this in memory of me.”
Whenever you eat the bread and drink the cup, you’re announcing the Lord’s death until he comes again.
So eat the bread and drink the cup of the Lord in the right way. Don’t do it in a way that isn’t worthy of him. If you do, you’ll be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
Everyone should examine themselves carefully before they eat the bread and drink from the cup.
Whoever eats and drinks must recognize the body of Christ. If they don’t, they’ll bring judgment upon themselves.
That’s why many of you are weak and sick, and a number of you have died.
We should think more carefully about what we’re doing. Then we wouldn’t be found guilty for this.
Still, when the Lord judges us in this way, he’s correcting us so that we won’t be judged in the end along with the rest of the world.
My brothers and sisters, when you meet for the Lord’s Supper, you should all eat together.
Anyone who’s hungry should eat something at home first. That way, when you meet together, you won’t be judged. When I come, I’ll give you more directions.

verses.heading: The Question About Gifts of the Holy Spirit / The Question About Gifts of the Holy Spirit
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I want you to know how the Holy Spirit works.
You know that before you were believers, you were somehow drawn away to worship idols that couldn’t even speak.
So I want you to know that anyone who’s speaking with the help of God’s Spirit never says, “May Jesus be cursed.” And without the help of the Holy Spirit, no one can say, “Jesus is Lord.”
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit distributes them.
There are different ways to serve, but they all come from the same Lord.
There are different ways the Spirit works, but the same God is working in all these ways and in every person.
The Holy Spirit is given to each of us in a special way for the good of all.
To one person, the Spirit gives a message of wisdom. To another, the same Spirit gives a message of knowledge.
To another the same Spirit gives faith, and to another gifts of healing.

To another he gives the power to do miracles, or to prophesy, or to tell spirits apart, or to speak in different kinds of languages they hadn’t known before. And to still others he gives the ability to explain what was said in those languages.
All these gifts are produced by one and the same Spirit. He gives gifts to each person, just as he decides.

verses.heading: One Body but Many Parts
verses.text: The body has many parts, but all of its many parts make up that one body. It’s the same with Christ.
We were all baptized by one Spirit into one body. It didn’t matter whether we were Jews or Gentiles, slaves or free people. We were all given the same Spirit to drink.
So the body is not made up of just one part. It has many parts.
If the foot said, “I’m not a hand, so I don’t belong to the body,” that wouldn’t make it not part of the body anymore.
And if the ear said, “I’m not an eye, so I don’t belong to the body,” that wouldn’t make it not part of the body anymore.
If the whole body were an eye, how could it hear? If the whole body were an ear, how could it smell?
God has placed each part in the body just as he wanted it to be.
If all the parts were the same, how could there be a body?
As it is, there are many parts, but there’s only one body.
The eye can’t say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” The head can’t say to the feet, “I don’t need you!”
It’s just the opposite! The parts of the body that seem to be weaker are the ones we can’t do without.
Any parts that we think are less attractive, we take special care to dress up. Some parts are private, and we treat them with modesty,
which the other parts don’t need. When God put the body together, he gave more honor to the parts that didn’t have any.
He did that so the parts of the body wouldn’t divide into opposing groups. Instead, they would all take care of one another.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it. If one part is honored, every part shares in its joy.
You are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
God has placed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, helping, guiding, and speaking in different kinds of languages.
Is everyone an apostle? Is everyone a prophet? Is everyone a teacher? Do all work miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in languages they hadn’t known before? Do all explain what is said in those languages?
Above all, you should want the greater gifts, but now let me show you the best way of all.

verses.heading: Love Is the Greatest of All
verses.subheading: Love Is the Greatest of All
verses.text: If I speak in the languages of human beings or even of angels, but I don’t have love, I’m only a loud gong or a noisy cymbal.
If I have the gift of prophecy and can understand all the secret things of God and know everything about him, and if I have enough faith to move mountains, but I don’t have love, I’m nothing at all.
If I give everything I have to the poor, and I endure so much hardship that I can brag about it, but I don’t have love, that doesn’t do me any good at all.
Love is patient and kind. It doesn’t want what belongs to other people. It doesn’t brag, it isn’t proud,
and it doesn’t treat other people with disrespect. Love doesn’t look out for its own interests. It doesn’t become angry easily. It doesn’t keep track of other people’s wrongs.
Love takes no joy in bad things happening, but it’s full of joy when the truth prevails.
Love always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always endures.
Love never fails. But prophecies will end; unknown languages will go silent; knowledge will disappear.
Now we know only in part, and we prophesy only in part.
But when what is complete arrives, the things that are not complete will disappear.
When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, and I had the understanding of a child. But when I became a man, I put the ways of childhood behind me.

Now we see only a dim reflection of things, as if we were seeing them in a foggy mirror. But someday we will see clearly, face to face. Now I know in part; then I will know completely, just as God knows me completely.
These three things will never end: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is love.

verses.heading: Worship in a Way That Helps People Understand
verses.subheading: Worship in a Way That Helps People Understand
verses.text: So follow the way of love, and be eager to have the gifts of the Spirit. Most of all, you should want the gift of prophecy.
Anyone who speaks in an unknown language doesn’t speak to people. They speak only to God. In fact, no one understands them, because what they say by the Spirit remains a mystery.
But the person who prophesies speaks to people and makes them stronger, gives them hope, and comforts them.
Those who speak in unknown languages build up only themselves. But the person who prophesies builds up the church.

I’d like all of you to speak in unknown languages, but I’d rather have you prophesy. The person who prophesies is more helpful than the one who speaks in an unknown language, unless someone explains what they’re saying; then the whole church can be built up.
Brothers and sisters, if I came to you and spoke in an unknown language, what good would that do? If I really wanted to help you, I’d come with a revelation or insight or prophecy or teaching.
Think about a musical instrument such as a flute or a harp. No one will know what the tune is unless the notes are played distinctly.
In the army, if the bugler didn’t play the call clearly, who would get ready for battle?
It’s the same with you. You must speak words that people understand. If you don’t, no one will know what you’re saying. You’ll just be speaking into the air.
It is true that there are all kinds of languages in the world and they all have meaning.
But if I don’t understand what someone is saying, I’m a stranger to the person speaking, and that person is a stranger to me.
It’s the same with you. Since you’re eager to have the gifts of the Spirit, do your best to use the gifts that build up the church.
So anyone who speaks in an unknown language should pray that they’ll be able to explain what they say.
