If I pray in an unknown language, my spirit is praying, but my mind is idle.
So what should I do? I’ll pray with my spirit, but I’ll also pray with my understanding. I’ll sing with my spirit, but I’ll also sing with my understanding.
Otherwise, if you’re thanking God in the Spirit and there are visitors present who want to know what’s going on, how can they say “Amen” when you give thanks? They don’t know what you’re saying.
You might be giving thanks, but no one else is being built up.
I thank God that I speak in unknown languages more than all of you.
But in the church, I’d rather speak five words in a language people can understand, in order to teach them, than 10,000 words in an unfamiliar language.
Brothers and sisters, stop thinking like children. Be like babies as far as evil is concerned, but in your thinking, be like adults.
In the law it is written, “With unfamiliar languages and through the lips of outsiders I will speak to these people. But even then they won’t listen to me.” That is what the Lord says.
So speaking in unknown languages is a sign for those who don’t believe, not for those who do believe. But prophecy is for those who believe, not for those who don’t.
Suppose the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in unknown languages. If visitors or unbelievers come in, won’t they say that you’re out of your minds?

But if unbelievers or visitors come in while everyone is prophesying, they’ll feel as if they’re being questioned; the secrets of their hearts will be brought out into the open; and they’ll realize they’ve been doing wrong. Then they’ll fall down and worship God and exclaim, “God is really here among you!”

verses.heading: Proper Worship
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, what should we say then? When you come together, each of you should bring something—a hymn, a teaching, a revelation, a message in another language, or an explanation of what was said in another language. Everything must be done to build up the church.
No more than two or three people should speak in another language, and they should speak one at a time. Then someone must explain what was said.
But if there’s no one to explain, they should keep quiet in the church and only speak to themselves and to God.
Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should evaluate what they say.
If a message comes from God to someone else who’s sitting there, the one who’s speaking should stop and let them speak.
Those who prophesy should all take turns. In that way, everyone can be taught and encouraged.
Prophets are able to control their own spirits.
God is not a God of disorder; he’s a God of peace, as in all the churches of the Lord’s people.
Women should remain silent in church meetings. They’re not allowed to speak. They must follow the lead of those who are in authority, as the law says.
If they have a question about something, they should ask their own husbands at home. It’s not proper for women to speak in church meetings.
Or did the word of God begin with you? Or are you the only people it has reached?
If anyone thinks they’re a prophet or that they have other gifts from the Spirit, they should agree that what I’m writing to you is the Lord’s command.
But anyone who doesn’t recognize this will not be recognized.
Brothers and sisters, you should be eager to prophesy, and you shouldn’t stop people from speaking in unknown languages.
But everything should be done in a proper and orderly way.

verses.heading: The Question About Rising From the Dead / The Question About Rising From the Dead
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I want to remind you of the good news that I preached to you. You received it, you belong to it,
and you’re being saved by it. But you must hold firmly to the message I preached to you. Otherwise, you’ll have believed it for nothing.
When I passed on to you what I received, I told you that the most important thing was that Christ died for our sins, just as Scripture said he would;
that he was buried; and that he was raised from the dead on the third day, just as Scripture said he would be.
He appeared to Peter, then he appeared to the 12 apostles,
and after that, he appeared to more than 500 brothers and sisters at the same time. (Most of them are still living, although some have died.)
He appeared to James, then he appeared to all the apostles,
and last of all he also appeared to me, as if I’d been born almost too late to see him.
I’m the least important of the apostles, and I’m not even fit to be called an apostle, because I tried to destroy God’s church.
But by the grace of God, I am what I am, and his grace wasn’t wasted on me. No, I worked harder than all the other apostles—though it wasn’t me doing the work. God’s grace was with me.
But whether it’s me or the other apostles, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.

verses.heading: Believers Will Rise From the Dead
verses.subheading: Believers Will Rise From the Dead
verses.text: But since we do preach that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that no one rises from the dead?
If no one rises from the dead, then Christ hasn’t been raised.
And if Christ hasn’t been raised, then what we preach doesn’t mean anything, and your faith doesn’t mean anything either.
Even worse, that would make us false witnesses about God, because we testified that God raised Christ from the dead. But God didn’t do that if the dead aren’t really raised.
If the dead aren’t raised, then Christ hasn’t been raised either.
And if Christ hasn’t been raised, then your faith doesn’t mean anything. Your sins haven’t been forgiven,
and those who have died believing in Christ are lost.
If we have hope in Christ only for this life, then people should pity us more than anyone else.
But Christ truly has been raised from the dead. He is the first of all those who will rise from the dead.
Since death came because of what one man did, rising from the dead also comes because of what one man did.
Because of Adam, all people die, and because of Christ, all will be made alive.
But this will happen in a particular order. Christ is the first of those who rise from the dead. When he comes back, those who belong to him will be raised.
And then the end will come, when he will hand the kingdom over to God the Father, after he has destroyed all other rulers, authorities, and powers.
Christ must rule until he has put all his enemies under his control.
The last enemy that will be destroyed is death.

Scripture says that God “has put everything under his control.” (When it says that “everything” has been put under him, it’s clear that this doesn’t include God himself, who put everything under Christ.)
When he has put everything under his control, the Son will then put himself under the rule of God, who put everything under him. In that way, God will be all in all.
If no one rises from the dead, where does that leave people who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
And why would we put ourselves in danger every hour?
I face death every day, just as surely as I take pride in what Christ Jesus our Lord has done for you through my work.
If I fought wild animals in Ephesus with nothing more than human hopes, then what did I gain by that? If the dead aren’t raised, “Let us eat and drink, because tomorrow we’ll die.”
Don’t let anyone fool you. “Having bad friends turns a good person into a bad one.”
Come back to your senses and stop sinning. Some of you don’t know anything about God. You should be ashamed of that!

verses.heading: The Body That Rises From the Dead
verses.subheading: The Body That Rises From the Dead
verses.text: But someone may ask, “How are the dead raised? What kind of body will they have?”
How foolish! What you plant doesn’t come to life unless it dies.
When you plant something, you don’t put a completely grown plant into the ground. You plant only a seed, maybe of wheat or something else.
But God gives the seed a body just as he has planned, and to each kind of seed he gives its own body.
Not all earthly creatures are the same. People have one kind of body, animals have another kind, birds another, and fish still another.
There are also heavenly bodies as well as earthly bodies. Heavenly bodies have one kind of glory, and earthly bodies have a different kind.
The sun has one kind of brightness, the moon has another kind, and stars have still another. And one star’s brightness is different from that of another star.
It will be like that with bodies that are raised from the dead. The body that is planted doesn’t last forever; the body that is raised from the dead does.
It is planted without honor, but it is raised in glory. It is planted in weakness, but it is raised in power.
It is planted as a body made alive in the natural way, but it is raised as a body made alive by spirit. Just as there is a naturally living body, there is also a spiritually living body.
It is written, “The first man Adam became a living person.” But the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
What is animated by spirit didn’t come first; the natural came first. What is spiritual came after that.
The first man came from the dust of the earth, but the second man came from heaven.
Those who belong to the earth are like the one who came from the earth, and those who are spiritual are like the one who came from heaven.
Right now we’re like the earthly man, but one day we’ll be like the heavenly man.
Brothers and sisters, here’s what I’m telling you. Bodies made of flesh and blood can’t inherit the kingdom of God. Things that perish can’t share in what never perishes.
Listen! I’m telling you a mystery. We’re not all going to die, but we will all be changed.
That will happen in a flash, as quickly as you can blink an eye. It will happen at the blast of the last trumpet. Then the dead will be raised to live forever, and we will be changed.

Our bodies that don’t last forever must be dressed with what does last forever. These bodies that perish must be dressed with what doesn’t perish, and these bodies that don’t last must be dressed with what lasts forever.
And when our bodies that die are dressed with what doesn’t die, then the saying that is written will come true, “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
“Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?”
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

My dear brothers and sisters, remain strong in the faith. Don’t let anything move you. Always give yourselves completely to the work of the Lord, because you know that in the Lord, your work isn’t for nothing.

verses.heading: The Question About the Offering for the Lord’s People / The Question About the Offering for the Lord’s People
verses.text: Now I want to deal with the offering of money for the Lord’s people. Do what I told the churches in Galatia to do.

On the first day of every week, each of you should put some money aside. The amount should be in keeping with how much you’ve made. Save up the money so you won’t have to take an offering when I come.
When I arrive, I’ll send some people with your gift to Jerusalem. They’ll be people you trust. You can choose them yourselves. I’ll give them letters to explain who they are.
If it seems good for me to go to Jerusalem too, they can travel with me.

verses.heading: What Paul Asks for Himself / What Paul Asks for Himself
verses.text: After I go through Macedonia, I’ll come and see you, since I’ll only be passing through Macedonia.
I might stay with you for a while, and even spend the winter. Then you can help me on my journey, wherever I go after that.
I don’t want to see you now while I’m just passing through. Instead, I want to spend some time with you, if the Lord allows that.
But I’m going to stay here in Ephesus until the day of Pentecost.
A door has opened wide for me to do some good work here, even though there are also many people who oppose me.
When Timothy comes, make sure he has nothing to worry about while he’s with you. He’s doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.
So don’t let anyone treat him with disrespect. Send him on his way in peace so he can return to me. I’m expecting him to come back along with the others.
As for our brother Apollos, I tried my best to get him to come to you with the others, but he really didn’t want to. He’ll come when it’s a better time.
Be on your guard, remain strong in the faith, be brave,
and be loving in everything you do.
You know that the first believers in Achaia were from the family of Stephanas. They’ve spent all their time serving the Lord’s people. Brothers and sisters, I’m asking you
to follow the lead of people like them. Follow everyone who joins in the task and works hard at it.
I was glad when Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus arrived. They have provided me with what you couldn’t give me.
They refreshed my spirit, and yours also. People like them are worthy of honor.

verses.heading: Final Greetings / Final Greetings
verses.text: The churches in the province of Asia send you their greetings. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets in their house.
All the brothers and sisters here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
I, Paul, am writing this greeting with my own hand.
If anyone does not love the Lord, let a curse be on that person! Come, Lord!
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
I give my love to all of you who belong to Christ Jesus. Amen.
From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and from Timothy our brother. To the members of God’s church in Corinth and to all of God’s holy people everywhere in southern Greece.
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.

verses.heading: Paul in the Province of Asia: God Gives Comfort / Paul in the Province of Asia: God Gives Comfort
verses.text: May the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ be praised! He’s a Father who’s filled with compassion.
He’s the God who gives all comfort, comforting us in all our troubles. As a result, we can comfort others when they’re in trouble, using the comfort that we’ve received from God.
We share very much in the sufferings of Christ, but we also share very much in his comfort.
If we’re distressed, it’s so that you can be comforted and renewed. If we’re comforted, it’s so that you can be comforted. Then you’ll be able to endure the same suffering that we’ve gone through.
Even though you’re suffering just as we are, we’re confident that God will comfort you, just as he’s comforting us.
Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the difficulties we went through in the province of Asia. We were in great distress—far more than we could stand. We even thought we were going to die.
In fact, we felt as if we’d actually been sentenced of death. But that happened so that we wouldn’t depend on ourselves, but on God who raises the dead to life.
God saved us from those deadly dangers, and he will do it again. We have confidence that he will continue to save us,
especially as you help us by praying for us. Then many people will give thanks to God for the kindness he has shown us in answer to many people’s prayers.

verses.heading: Paul Changes His Plans
verses.text: With God’s help, we’ve acted toward everyone, and especially toward you, honorably and honestly. We can say that with pride and a clear conscience. We’ve depended on God’s grace and not on the world’s wisdom.
We haven’t written anything to you that you couldn’t understand when you read it.

Up to this point you’ve only understood some of the things we’ve said. But I hope you’ll come to understand us completely. Then you’ll realize that you can be just as proud of us as we will be of you on the day when the Lord Jesus returns.
Because I was sure of this, I wanted to visit you before I went to Macedonia so that we could see each other twice.
I planned to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and then I was going to come back from there and see you again. After that you could have sent me on my way to Judea.
Was I not serious when I planned all that? Do I make my plans in the way the world does, so that in the same breath I say “Yes, yes” and “No, no”?
Just as surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
Silas, Timothy, and I preached to you about the Son of God, Jesus Christ, and he is not “Yes” and “No.” He’s always “Yes,”
because if you ask, “Did God keep his promises?” the answer in every case is, “Yes, through Jesus.” And so through him we say “Amen,” to the glory of God.
God makes us stand firm with you in Christ. He has anointed us, he has sealed us,
and he has put his Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee that he’ll give us everything else he promised.
But, as you know, I didn’t come to Corinth on my way to Macedonia. I stayed away because I wanted to spare you. (God is my witness that this was the reason—may he take my life if I’m lying!)
Not that we would ever treat you harshly as believers; you’re strong in your own faith, and we work together with you for your joy.
But I made up my mind not to have another painful visit with you.
If I made you sad, there wouldn’t be anyone left to make me happy.
I wrote the way I did so that when I came, you wouldn’t make me sad when you’re supposed to make me happy. I was sure that you would all want the same things I wanted.
I wrote to you in great distress, with a heavy heart, and with my eyes full of tears. I wasn’t trying to upset you. I just wanted you to know how deeply I love you.

verses.heading: Forgive the One Who Did Wrong
verses.subheading: Forgive the One Who Did Wrong
verses.text: If anyone has hurt me, he hasn’t just hurt me; he’s hurt all of you (in some sense—not to put it too strongly).
But when the majority of you decided to punish him, what you did was enough.
Now you should forgive him and comfort him. That way he won’t be so discouraged that he gives up.
I’m asking you to let him know that you still love him.
I wrote to you the way I did to see if you would pass the test and obey everything I asked you to do.
But now, anyone you forgive, I also forgive. And what I’ve forgiven—whatever there is to forgive—I’ve forgiven for your sakes, knowing that Christ is watching.
We don’t want Satan to outsmart us. We know how he does his evil work.

verses.heading: Paul’s Journey to Macedonia: Servants of the New Covenant / Paul’s Journey to Macedonia: Servants of the New Covenant
verses.text: When I went to Troas to preach the good news about Christ, I found that the Lord had opened a door of opportunity for me.
Even so, I didn’t have any peace of mind, because I couldn’t find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to the believers at Troas and went on to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always leads us as if we were prisoners in Christ’s victory parade. He uses us to spread the knowledge of Christ everywhere like perfume.
God considers us to be the aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are being lost.
To those who are being lost, we are the aroma of death. But to those who are being saved, we are the aroma of life. Who is able to do this kind of work?
Unlike many people, we aren’t selling God’s word to make money. It’s just the opposite! Because of Christ, we speak honestly before God, as people God has truly sent.
Are we beginning to praise ourselves again? Do we need a letter of recommendation, either to you or from you?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, where everyone can see it and read it.

It’s clear that you’re a letter from Christ, the result of our work for God, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God. You’re a letter not written on tablets of stone but on human hearts.
Through Christ, we can be sure of this before God.
By ourselves, we aren’t able to claim anything for ourselves. The power to do what we do comes from God.
He has given us the power to serve under a new covenant. It’s not based on the written Law of Moses; it comes from the Holy Spirit. The written Law kills, but the Spirit gives life.

verses.heading: The Greater Glory of the New Covenant
verses.subheading: The Greater Glory of the New Covenant
verses.text: The Law was written in letters on stone. Though it was a way of serving God, it led to death. But that way of serving God was surrounded by glory when it was introduced. The glory lasted for only a short time, but even so, the people of Israel couldn’t look at Moses’ face for very long because of it.
Wouldn’t the work of the Holy Spirit be even more glorious?
If the law that condemns people to death had glory, how much more glorious will the work of the Spirit be! It makes people right with God.
The glory of the old covenant is nothing compared with the far greater glory of the new covenant.
The glory of the old covenant lasted for only a short time. How much greater is the glory of the new covenant that lasts forever!
Since we have that kind of hope, we are very bold.
We aren’t like Moses, who used to cover his face with a veil to keep the people of Israel from seeing the last bit of glory fade away.
But they still don’t understand; to this day, the same veil remains when the old covenant is read. The veil has not been removed, because only in Christ is it taken away.
Even to this day, when the Law of Moses is read, a veil covers the minds of those who hear it.
But when anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

None of our faces are covered with a veil. All of us can see and contemplate the Lord’s glory. So we’re being changed to become more and more glorious like him. All this comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

verses.heading: A Treasure in Clay Jars
verses.text: So, because we have this work to do through God’s mercy, we don’t give up.

Instead, we refuse to do secret and shameful things. We don’t trick anyone, and we don’t twist God’s word. We do just the opposite! We present the truth plainly so that everyone can judge us in their own conscience before God.
Our good news may still be hidden behind a veil for those who are being lost.
The god of this world has blinded the minds of unbelievers so that they can’t see the light of the good news that makes Christ’s glory clear. He is the image of God.
The message we preach isn’t about ourselves. It’s about Jesus Christ as Lord, and about ourselves as your servants for his sake.
God said, “Let light shine out of darkness.” And he made his light shine in our hearts to give us the light we needed to know God’s glory, which is shown in the face of Christ.
But we’re like clay jars that hold a valuable treasure. We carry the good news around in these earthly bodies of ours to show that its mighty power comes from God and not from us.
We’re pressured from every side, but we never get crushed. Sometimes we don’t know which way to turn, but we never give up.
People might attack us, but God never abandons us. We can get knocked down, but we’re never knocked out.
We always carry around the death of Jesus in our bodies. In that way, the life of Jesus can be shown in our bodies.
Though we’re alive, we’re always threatened by death because we’re serving Jesus. This happens so that his life can be shown in our earthly bodies.
So death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
It is written, “I believed, and so I’ve spoken.” We have that same spirit of faith, and so we also believe and speak.
We know that the same God who raised the Lord Jesus from the dead will also raise us up with Jesus and present both you and us to himself.
All this is for your benefit, so that grace will reach more and more people, and they will become more and more thankful and give glory to God.
That’s why we never give up. Though our bodies are becoming weaker and weaker, our spirits are being renewed day by day.
Our troubles are small and they last only for a short time, but they’re earning a glory for us that will last forever. That glory outweighs all our troubles.
So we don’t focus on what we can see. Instead, we focus on what we can’t see. That’s because the things that can be seen last only a short time, but the things that can’t be seen will last forever.

verses.heading: Waiting for Our New Bodies
verses.text: We know the earthly tent we live in will be destroyed. But we have a building made by God himself, a house not made by human hands. It lasts forever, waiting for us in heaven.
In the meantime, we groan because we want so much to put on our heavenly home.
It feels as if we’re wearing clothing now that’s falling off of us, and we want to wear clothes that won’t.

While we live in this tent of ours, we groan and feel weighed down. We don’t want our clothes to fall off. Instead, we want to be fully dressed with our heavenly home. That way the part of us that dies will be will swallowed up in life.
God made us for that very purpose, and he has given us the Holy Spirit as a down payment, a guarantee of what is still to come.
This gives us the confidence to keep living the way we do. We know that as long as we’re at home in our bodies, we’re away from the Lord.
We recognize this because we’re guided by faith, not by what we can see.
We live this way confidently, as I said, because we’d rather be away from our bodies and at home with the Lord.
So we try our best to make sure that he’ll be pleased with us, whether we’re at home in our bodies or away from them.
We must all stand before Christ to be judged, and then each of us will receive what we deserve for the things we did while we were in our bodies, whether they were good or bad.

verses.heading: Christ Brings Us Back to God
verses.subheading: Christ Brings Us Back to God
verses.text: Knowing we’re going to face judgment puts the fear of God in us, and we don’t pretend to anyone that we’re something we’re not. What we truly are is clear to God, and I hope that you’re clearly aware of it too.

We’re not trying to recommend ourselves to you again, but we are giving you a chance to be proud of us. That way you can answer those who judge people by external appearances, rather than by what’s in their hearts.
If we’re out of our minds, as some people say, that’s for the sake of God. And if we’re in our right minds, that’s for your sakes.
Christ’s love doesn’t give us any other choice. We’re convinced that one person died for everyone, and so everyone died.
Christ died for everyone so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died for them and was raised again.
So from now on we don’t look at anyone from the world’s point of view. Once we even looked at Christ that way, but we don’t anymore.
If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come. The old is gone! The new is here!
All this is from God, who brought us back to himself through Christ and gave us the task of bringing others back to him. God wants us to let them know that
God was bringing the world back to himself through Christ and not holding people’s sins against them. God has trusted us with this message about how people can be brought back to him.
So we are Christ’s official messengers. It’s as if God were making his appeal through us. So we beg you, on Christ’s behalf: Come back to God!
He never sinned, but God made him become sin for us, so that in him we could be made right with God.
As people who work together with God, we ask you not to receive God’s grace and then do nothing with it.
He says, “When I had mercy on you, I heard you. On the day I saved you, I helped you.” I tell you, now is the time when God is having mercy. Now is the day when he wants to save us.

verses.heading: Paul’s Sufferings
verses.text: We don’t put anything in anyone’s way, so no one should find fault with our work.
Instead, we try to show in every way that we’re genuine servants of God. We endure through troubles, hard times, and suffering.
We don’t give up if we’re beaten or put in prison, or if people stir up trouble in the streets. We work hard and go without sleep or food if we have to.
We live pure lives. We’re understanding, patient, and kind. We serve God in the Holy Spirit and with true love
and honesty. We use the power of God, holding the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and the left.
We serve God in times of glory and shame, whether the things people say about us are good or bad. We’re genuine, but people treat us as if we were fakes.
We’re well known, but people treat us as if we were unknown. We’re dying, but we continue to live. We’re beaten, but we’re not killed.
We’re often distressed, but we’re always full of joy. We’re poor, but we make many people rich. We own nothing, but we never lack anything.
Dear friends in Corinth, we’ve spoken freely to you, and we’ve opened our hearts wide.
We’re not holding back our love from you. But you’re holding back your love from us.
I speak to you as if you were my own children. It’s only fair that you also open your hearts wide to us.

verses.heading: Paul Warns Against Worshiping False Gods
verses.subheading: Paul Warns Against Worshiping False Gods
verses.text: Don’t be joined together with unbelievers. What do right and wrong have in common? Can light and darkness be friends?
How can Christ and Satan agree? What does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?

How can the temple of the true God get along with idols? We are the temple of the living God, as God has said, “I will live with them and walk among them, and I will be their God and they will be my people.”
Therefore, “Come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Don’t touch anything that isn’t clean, and then I’ll receive you.”
And, “I’ll be a Father to you, and you’ll be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”
Dear friends, since we have these promises from God, let’s purify ourselves from everything that could make our bodies and spirits impure. Let’s be completely holy, to honor God.

verses.heading: Paul Rejoices When the Church Turns Away From Sin
verses.subheading: Paul Rejoices When the Church Turns Away From Sin
verses.text: Make room for us in your hearts. We haven’t cheated anyone, we haven’t corrupted anyone, and we haven’t taken advantage of anyone.
I don’t say this to accuse you; I’ve told you before that you mean so much to us that we would live or die with you.
I’ve spoken to you very honestly. I’m very proud of you. I’m truly encouraged; even with all of our troubles, I’m overflowing with joy.
When we came to Macedonia, we weren’t able to rest. There was trouble all around. We had battles on the outside and fears on the inside.
But God, who comforts those who are discouraged, comforted us by sending Titus.

We were comforted by his arrival, and also by the comfort you had given him. He told us how much you longed for me and about your deep sadness and great concern for me. That made me happier than ever.
Even if my letter upset you, I’m not sorry that I sent it. At first I was sorry, because I see that my letter hurt you, though only for a little while.
But now I’m happy, not because I made you sad, but because your sadness led you to turn away from your sins. You felt sad the right way as God intended, so we didn’t hurt you in any way.
Godly sadness causes us to turn away from our sins and be saved. And we’re certainly not sorry about that! But worldly sadness brings death.

Look at what that godly sadness has produced in you. You’re working hard to clear yourselves. You’re upset and alarmed. You’re longing to see me. You’re concerned about what has happened. You want to make sure that the right thing is done. In every way, you’ve shown that you’re not at fault.

So even though I wrote to you, it wasn’t for the sake of the one who did the wrong or for the sake the one who was wronged. Instead, I wrote you so that in the sight of God you could see for yourselves how faithful you are to us.
All of this is very encouraging. We were also very glad to see how happy Titus was. You have all refreshed his spirit.
I had bragged about you to him, and you haven’t let me down. Everything we said to you was true, and in the same way, everything we told Titus about you has also turned out to be true.
His love for you is even greater when he remembers how you all obeyed. You received him with fear and trembling.
I’m glad I can have complete confidence in you.

verses.heading: Paul in Macedonia: Giving Freely to the Lord’s People / Paul in Macedonia: Giving Freely to the Lord’s People
verses.text: And now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace that God has given to the churches in Macedonia.
They were going through a great trial, but they were still overflowing with joy, so that even though they were very poor, they gave generously.
I assure you that they gave as much as they could. They gave even more than they could spare. Completely on their own,
they begged us for the privilege of serving the Lord’s people by sharing with them in that way.
They did more than we expected. First they gave themselves to the Lord, and then they gave themselves to us by the will of God.
Titus has already started collecting money from you, so we’ve asked him to help you finish making your kind gift.
Since you do so well in everything else—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in eagerness, and in the love we taught you—make sure that you also do well in the grace of giving to others.
I’m not commanding you to do this. But I do want to challenge you to show how sincere your love is compared with the eagerness of others.
You know how generous our Lord Jesus Christ was. Even though he was rich, he became poor for your sake, so that because he became poor, you would become rich.
Here’s what I think would be the best thing for you to do. Last year you were the first ones to give, and you were even the first ones to want to give.
So finish the work. Then the desire you had to do it will be matched by the way you’ve finished it. Give based on how much you have.
Do you really want to give? Then your gift will be measured by what you have, not by what you don’t.
We don’t want others to have it easy while you are burdened. We want things to be fair.
Right now you’re well off and you can help others with what they need. Later on they’ll be well off and they’ll be able to help you. That will make things fair for everyone.
It is written, “The one who gathered a lot didn’t have too much, and the one who gathered a little had enough.”

verses.heading: Paul Sends Titus to Corinth to Receive the Offering
verses.subheading: Paul Sends Titus to Corinth to Receive the Offering
verses.text: Titus has the same concern for you that I do. I thank God for putting that in his heart.
When we asked Titus to go and help you, he agreed eagerly. It was what he wanted to do himself.
Along with Titus, we’re sending another brother. He’s someone all the churches respect for what he has done for the good news.
The churches chose him to come along with us as we collect the offering and bring it to Jerusalem. We’re carrying out this work because we want to honor the Lord and show how ready we are to help.
We don’t want anyone to have any reason to criticize how we’re taking care of this generous gift.
So we’re trying hard to do what both the Lord and people will see as right.
We’re also sending another one of our brothers with these two. This man has often proved to us in many ways how committed he is. He’s even more committed now because he has great confidence in you.
Titus is my helper, and he and I work together among you; our brothers are messengers from the churches who honor Christ.
So show them and all the churches how much you love others and why we’re so proud of you.
I don’t really need to write to you about giving in order to help the Lord’s people.

I know how much you want to do that. I’ve been bragging about you to the people in Macedonia. I’ve been telling them that you who live in Achaia have been ready to give since last year. Your eagerness has stirred up most of them to give as well.
But I’m sending the brothers so that our bragging about you will prove to be true and you’ll be ready, just as I said you’d be.
If people from Macedonia come with me and discover that you’re not ready, then we’ll be embarrassed for having been so confident about you. And you’ll be even more embarrassed!

So I thought I should encourage the brothers to visit you in advance and help you finish collecting the generous gift you had promised. Then it will be ready as a gift that’s freely given, not as one that’s given reluctantly.

verses.heading: Paul’s Advice to Give Freely
verses.text: Remember this: The one who plants only a little will gather only a little, but the one who plants a lot will gather a lot.
Each of you should give what you’ve decided in your heart to give. You shouldn’t give if you don’t want to. You shouldn’t give because you feel you have to. God loves it when you’re glad to give.
And God is able to bless you so much that you’ll always have everything you need, and in that way, you’ll be able to do more and more good works.
It is written, “They have spread their gifts around to the poor. Their good works continue forever.”
God, who supplies seed for planting and bread for eating, will also supply and increase the amount of your seed and the good works that grow from it.
You’ll be made rich in every way so that you can always give freely. We will bring your generous gifts to the people who need them, and they’ll give thanks to God.
Your gifts will meet the needs of the Lord’s people, but that’s not all. They will also cause many people to thank God.

You will have shown that you’re dependable by what you’ve given. Other people will praise God because you’ve obeyed him and shown that you really do believe the good news about Christ. They’ll also praise God because you’ve shared so freely with them and with everyone else.
They’ll pray for you with hearts full of gratitude because God has given you so much grace.
Thanks be to God for his gift, which is so great that words can’t describe it!

verses.heading: Paul Heading for Corinth: Defending His Ministry / Paul Heading for Corinth: Defending His Ministry
verses.text: I appeal to you by the humbleness and gentleness of Christ—I, Paul, the one you think is timid when I’m face to face with you, but bold when I’m away from you.
When I come to see you, please don’t make me be as severe as I expect I’ll need to be toward some people who think I live in the same way as the people of this world.
I do live in the world, but I don’t fight my battles the way the people of the world do.
The weapons I fight with aren’t the weapons of this world. They’re just the opposite! They use the power of God to destroy resistance—
every argument and every arrogant assumption that keeps people from knowing God. They take every thought captive and make it obedient to Christ.
We’ll be ready to punish anyone who still tries to disobey once the whole church has chosen to obey.
You’re judging only by how things look on the surface. If someone is confident that they belong to Christ, they should consider again that we belong to Christ just as much as they do.
So even if I brag too much about the authority the Lord has given me to build you up, not to tear you down, I’m not ashamed of that kind of bragging.
Don’t think that I’m trying to scare you with my letters.
Some say, “In his letters, he sounds important and forceful, but in person he’s not very impressive, and he’s not a good speaker.”
People who say that should realize that whatever I say in my letters when I’m away from you, I will do in my actions when I’m with you.
I’m not going to compare myself with those other people who praise themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they’re not being wise.
But I won’t brag any more than I should. I’ll only brag about what I’ve done in the area of service that God himself assigned to me.
That area includes you, so I’m not going too far in my bragging, as I would be if I hadn’t come to where you live. But I did get there with the good news about Christ.
And I won’t brag about the work that others have done. If I did, I’d be bragging more than I should. I hope that my work among you will greatly increase as your faith continues to grow.
Then I’ll be able to preach the good news in the areas beyond you. I don’t want to brag about work that’s already been done in someone else’s territory.
Instead, “The one who brags should brag about what the Lord has done.”
It’s not the ones who praise themselves who are accepted—it’s the ones the Lord praises.

verses.heading: Paul and the False Apostles
verses.text: I hope you’ll put up with a little foolishness on my part. Yes, please put up with me!
I’m jealous for you with a godly jealousy. I promised you to one husband, Christ, to give you to him like a pure virgin bride.
But just as Eve’s mind was tricked by the snake’s clever lies, I’m afraid that your minds will also be led astray somehow from your true and pure love for Christ.

If someone comes to you and preaches about a Jesus who’s different from the Jesus we preached about, or a spirit different from the Spirit you received, or a version of the good news that’s different from the one you accepted, you put up with those kinds of things easily enough.
I don’t think I’m the least bit inferior those “super-apostles.”
It’s true that I haven’t been trained as a speaker, but I do have knowledge. I’ve made that perfectly clear to you in every way.
I preached God’s good news to you free of charge. When I did that, I was humbling myself in order to lift you up. Was that a sin?
I received help from other churches so I could serve you. That was almost like robbing them.

When I was with you and needed something, I didn’t make you pay for it. The believers who came from Macedonia provided everything I needed. I haven’t made you pay for anything at all, and I won’t ever do that.
As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, nobody in Achaia will keep me from being proud of this.
Why? Because I don’t love you? No! God knows that I do!
And I’m going to keep on doing what I’ve been doing, in order to discredit the people who think they should be considered equal with us.
People like that are false apostles and dishonest workers. They’re only pretending to be apostles of Christ.
But that comes as no surprise. Even Satan himself pretends to be an angel of light.
So it shouldn’t surprise us if Satan’s servants also pretend to be serving God. But in the end, they’ll get exactly what they deserve.

verses.heading: Paul Brags About His Sufferings
verses.text: I’ll say it again: Nobody should think I’m a fool. But if you do, put up with me just as you would put up with a fool, so I can do a little bragging.
When I brag about myself like this, I’m not talking the way the Lord would. I’m talking like a fool.
But since many others are bragging the way the people of the world do, let me show you that I can brag like them too.
You gladly put up with fools because you’re so wise!
In fact, you even put up with anyone who makes you a slave or uses you or takes advantage of you. You put up with those who claim to be better than you, and even with those who slap you in the face.
I’m ashamed to say that I was too weak for that! Whatever anyone else dares to brag about— I’m speaking like a fool—I also dare to brag about.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Do they belong to the people of Israel? So do I. Are they Abraham’s children? So am I.

Are they serving Christ? I’m serving him even more. (I’m out of my mind to talk like this!) I’ve worked much harder. I’ve been in prison more often. I’ve suffered terrible beatings. Again and again I’ve almost died.
Five times the Jews gave me 39 strokes with a whip.
Three times I was beaten with sticks. Once they tried to kill me by throwing stones at me. Three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

I’ve had to keep on the move constantly. I’ve been in danger from rivers, in danger from robbers, in danger from my fellow Jews, and in danger from Gentiles. I’ve been in danger in the city, in the country, and at sea. I’ve been in danger from people who pretended they were believers.
I’ve worked very hard and often gone without sleep. I’ve been hungry and thirsty and gone without food; I’ve been cold and lacked clothes.
And on top of everything else, every day I’ve felt the pressure of my concern for all the churches.
If anyone is weak, I feel weak. If anyone is led into sin, I burn on the inside.
If I have to brag, let me brag about the things that show how weak I am.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus—may he be praised forever—knows that I’m not lying.
In Damascus, the governor who served under King Aretas had the city locked down because he wanted to arrest me.
But I escaped by being lowered in a basket out a window in the city wall!

verses.heading: Paul’s Vision and His Painful Problem
verses.subheading: Paul’s Vision and His Painful Problem
verses.text: But now I’m going to go back to bragging, even though there’s nothing to be gained by it. I’m going to talk about visions and revelations from the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who was taken up to the third heaven 14 years ago. I don’t know whether his body was taken up or not—only God knows.

But I do know that this man was taken up into paradise, whether he was in his body or out of it—only God knows that. He heard things there that can’t be put into words, things that no human is allowed to repeat.
I’ll brag about a man like that, but I won’t brag about myself. I’ll only brag about how weak I am.
Even if I did decide to brag, that wouldn’t make me a fool, because I’d be telling the truth. But I don’t brag, so that no one will think more of me than they should based on what I say and do.

God has shown me amazing and wonderful things, but people shouldn’t think more of me because of those. In fact, so that I wouldn’t become overly proud, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger from Satan to harass me.
I begged the Lord three times to take it away from me.
But he told me, “My grace is all you need, because my power is made perfect in weakness.” So I will gladly brag all the more about how weak I am, so that Christ’s power can rest on me.
That is why, for Christ’s sake, I delight in weaknesses, insults, hard times, attacks, and difficulties. For when I’m weak, that’s when I’m strong.

verses.heading: Paul’s Concern for the People of Corinth
verses.subheading: Paul’s Concern for the People of Corinth
verses.text: I’ve made a fool of myself, but you forced me to. You should have been the ones to praise me. I’m not the least bit inferior to the “super-apostles,” even though I’m nothing.
While I was with you, I demonstrated the signs of a true apostle with great endurance, including signs, wonders, and miracles.
How did I treat you worse than any of the other churches? The only difference was that I didn’t make you pay for anything. Forgive me for that wrong!

Now I’m ready to visit you for the third time. I’m not going to be a burden to you, because I don’t want what you have. What I really want is you. After all, children shouldn’t have to save up for their parents. Parents should save up for their children.
So I’ll be very happy to spend everything I have for you. I will even spend myself. If I love you more, will you love me less?
But in any case, I haven’t caused you any expense. But being so clever, I’ve caught you by tricking you! Or so you think!
Did I take advantage of you through any of the men I sent to you?
I asked Titus to go to you, and I sent our brother with him. Titus didn’t take advantage of you, did he? Weren’t he and I guided by the same Spirit to do the very same kinds of things?

All this time, have you been thinking that I’ve been speaking up for myself? No, I’ve been speaking with God as my witness, as a believer in Christ. Dear friends, everything I do is to help you become stronger.

I’m afraid that when I come I won’t find you as I want you to be, and you won’t find me as you want me to be. I’m afraid that there will be arguing, jealousy, fits of anger, selfish ambition, insults, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.

I’m afraid that when I come my God will humble me before you. I’ll be grieved about many who have sinned earlier and who haven’t turned away from the impurity, sexual sin, and wild living that they’ve gotten involved in.

verses.heading: Final Warnings
verses.text: This will be my third visit to you. Scripture says, “Every matter must be proved by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
I already warned you during my second visit, and I’ll say it again now while I’m away: When I return, I won’t spare those who sinned earlier. I won’t spare any of the others, either,
since you’re asking me to prove that Christ is speaking through me. He isn’t weak in dealing with you. He’s powerful in your midst.

It’s true that Christ was nailed to the cross in weakness, but now he’s alive by God’s power. In the same way, we share his weakness, but by God’s power we’ll be alive with Christ as we deal with you.
Take a good look at yourselves to see if you really are believers. Test yourselves. Don’t you realize that Christ Jesus is in you? Unless, of course, you fail the test!
But I hope you’ll discover that I haven’t failed the test.
I pray to God that you won’t do anything wrong—not so that people will see that I’ve passed the test, but so that you will do what is right, even if it seems that I’ve failed.
I can’t do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
I’m glad whenever I’m weak but you’re strong. I pray that you will be fully restored.

That’s why I’m writing these things now, while I’m away. Then when I do come, I won’t have to use my authority and be hard on you. The Lord gave me that authority to build you up, not to tear you down.

verses.heading: Final Greetings / Final Greetings
verses.text: Finally, brothers and sisters, be joyful! Work to make everything right with one another. Encourage one another and agree with each other. Live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss.
All God’s people here send their greetings.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

From Paul, an apostle, and from all the brothers and sisters who are with me. I have not been sent by any human group or leader. I’ve been sent by Jesus Christ and by God the Father, who raised him from the dead. To the churches in Galatia.
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace. In obedience to the will of our God and Father,
Jesus gave his life for our sins. He did this to set us free from the evil age we’re now living in.
May God receive glory forever and ever! Amen.

verses.heading: There Is No Other Good News
verses.subheading: There Is No Other Good News
verses.text: I’m amazed that after such a short time, you’re abandoning the one who called you to live in the grace of Christ. You’re turning to a different “good news”—
which is not good news at all. It seems that some people have gotten you all confused by twisting the good news about Christ.

Don’t let anyone preach a “good news” to you that’s different from the one we first told you about. Don’t let us do that, and don’t let even an angel from heaven do it. If anyone does, let them fall under God’s curse!
I’ll say it again: If anyone preaches a “good news” to you that’s different from what you accepted, let them fall under God’s curse!

Now do I sound like somebody who wants people to think well of me? Or do I sound like somebody who wants God to think well of me? If I were still trying to please people, I wouldn’t be serving Christ.

verses.heading: Paul’s Good News Comes from God
verses.subheading: Paul’s Good News Comes from God
verses.text: I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that the good news I preached to you didn’t come from human beings.
Nobody gave it to me or taught it to me. Instead, Jesus Christ revealed it to me.
You’ve heard how I lived earlier as a follower of Judaism. I attacked the church of God mercilessly, and I tried to destroy it.
I had studied Judaism in depth, more so than most Jews my age. That was because I was so devoted to the teachings passed down from those who’d lived before us.
But God had set me apart before I was born and called me by his grace. When he was pleased
to reveal his Son in my life so I could preach about him to the Gentiles, I didn’t consult any human being.
I didn’t go up to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before I was. Instead, I went into Arabia. Later I returned to Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to get to know Peter. I stayed with him for 15 days.
I didn’t see any of the other apostles. I only saw James, the Lord’s brother.
As God is my witness, I’m telling you the truth.
Then I went to Syria and Cilicia.
The synagogues in Judea that believe in Christ had never seen me in person.
They’d only heard others say, “The man who used to attack us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”
And they praised God because of me.

verses.heading: Paul Is Accepted by the Apostles
verses.subheading: Paul Is Accepted by the Apostles
verses.text: Then after fourteen years I went up to Jerusalem again. This time I went with Barnabas. I also took Titus along.

I went because God showed me that he wanted me to go. I met privately with those who are respected as leaders. I presented to them the good news that I preach among the Gentiles. I wanted to be sure that it wasn’t useless for me to keep presenting the good news that way.
But even though Titus, who was with me, was Greek, they didn’t require him to be circumcised.
That question came up because some false believers had slipped in among us to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus. They wanted to make us slaves again.
But we didn’t give in to them for a moment, in order to protect the truth of the good news for you.

The people in Jerusalem who were considered to be important didn’t add anything to my message. (And it didn’t matter to me who they were anyway. God doesn’t see some people as more important than others.)
It was just the opposite! They recognized that I had been trusted with the task of preaching the good news to the Gentiles, just as Peter had been trusted with preaching to the Jews.
God was working through Peter as an apostle to the Jews, and God was working through me as an apostle to the Gentiles.

James, Peter, and John, who are respected as pillars in the church, recognized that God had given me this privilege. So they shook hands with Barnabas and me to welcome us as partners. They agreed that we should go to the Gentiles while they went to the Jews.
They asked only one thing: They wanted us to continue to remember the poor, which is what I had wanted to do all along.

verses.heading: Paul Opposes Peter
verses.text: But when Peter came to Antioch, I challenged him directly, because he was clearly wrong.

Before a group came representing James, Peter was eating with the Gentiles. But after they arrived, Peter pulled back and wouldn’t eat with them. He was afraid of those who wanted to require people to be circumcised.
He was being hypocritical, and the other Jews followed his example. Even Barnabas was led astray.

When I saw that they were not acting consistently with the truth of the good news, I spoke to Peter in front of everyone. I said, “You’re a Jew, but you live like a Gentile, not a Jew. So why are you trying force the Gentiles to follow Jewish ways?
“We grew up as Jews. We’re not sinful Gentiles.

But even though we’re used to following the law, we still know that no one can be made right with God that way. Instead, a person needs to believe in Jesus Christ. So we too have put our faith in Christ Jesus to be made right with God. We’re not trying to do that by obeying the law, because no one can be made right with God by obeying the law.
“But what if, as we seek to be made right with God through Christ, we Jews find ourselves to be sinners? Does that mean that Christ promotes sin? Certainly not!
But if I rebuild what I destroyed, then I would really be breaking the law.
“Through my experience with the law, I died to the law so that I might live for God.

I’ve been crucified with Christ. I’m not the one living anymore. Christ is living in me. I do continue to live in this body, but I do that by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
I don’t regard the grace of God as worthless. If a person could become right with God by obeying the law, then Christ died for nothing!”

verses.heading: Faith or Obeying the Law
verses.text: You foolish Galatians! Who cast a spell on you? When I preached, I showed you clearly that Jesus Christ had been nailed to the cross.
I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Holy Spirit by keeping the law, or by believing what you heard?
Are you so foolish? You began by the Spirit; are you now trying to finish by your own efforts?
Have you experienced so much for nothing? (If it really was for nothing.)
Let me ask again: Does God give you his Spirit and work miracles among you because you do what the law says? Or is it because you believe what you’ve heard?
In the same way, Abraham “believed God, and this was considered to make him right with God.”
So you should understand that people who have faith are children of Abraham.
Scripture saw long ago that God would make the Gentiles right with himself by faith. It announced the good news ahead of time to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”
So those who rely on faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
All who rely on obeying the law are under a curse. It is written, “Cursed is everyone who doesn’t continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”
We know that no one who relies on the law is made right with God, because “the one who is right with God will live by faith.”
The law isn’t based on faith. In fact, it’s just the opposite. The law says, “The person who does these things will live by them.”
Christ set us free from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. It is written, “Everyone who is hanged on a pole is under God’s curse.”
He set us free so that the blessing that was given to Abraham would come to the Gentiles through Christ Jesus. That way by faith we would receive the promised Holy Spirit.

verses.heading: The Law and the Promise
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, let me give you an example from everyday life. Once people make an official agreement, no one else can cancel it or change it.

It’s the same with the promises that God made to Abraham and to his seed. Scripture doesn’t say, “and to your seeds.” That would mean many people. It says, “and to your seed.” That means one person—Christ.
Here’s what I mean: The law was introduced 430 years after the covenant God made with Abraham. It can’t cancel their agreement or get rid of the promise.
If the benefits of this agreement depended on the law, then they would no longer depend on the promise. But God gave them to Abraham as a free gift through a promise.

Then why was the law given at all? It was added because of human sin. It was supposed to control us until the promised Seed came. The law was given through angels, and a mediator was put in charge of it.
When a mediator is involved, that means there’s more than one party to an agreement. But God didn’t use a mediator when he made his promise to Abraham.
So is the law opposed to God’s promises? Certainly not! If a law had been given that could give life, then people could become right with God by obeying that law.
But Scripture has locked up everything under the control of sin, so that what was promised could be given through faith in Jesus Christ to those who believe.

verses.heading: Children of God
verses.text: Before faith in Christ came, the law was guarding us. We were locked up while waiting for faith to appear.
So the law was put in charge of us until Christ came. He came so that we could be shown to be in the right because of faith.
But now that this faith has come, the law is no longer in charge of us.
So in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith.
All of you who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ as if he were new clothes.
There’s no longer any Jew or Gentile, slave or free, male or female, because you’re all one in Christ Jesus.
If you belong to Christ, then you’re Abraham’s seed, and you’ll receive what God has promised.
Here’s what I’ve been saying. As long as your own children are young, they’re no different from slaves in your house, even though they’re going to own all the property someday.
Other people take care of them and the property, until they become adults.
It’s the same with us. When we were children, we were slaves to the basic spiritual powers of the world.

But then the chosen time came, and God sent his Son. He was born to a woman, and he was born under the authority of the law. This was so he could set everyone free who was under the authority of the law.
He wanted us to be adopted as children, with all the rights that children have.
Because you are his children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts. This is the Spirit who calls out, “Abba, Father!”
verses.html: Because you are his children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts. This is the Spirit who calls out, “Abba, Father!”

verses.text: So you’re not a slave anymore, you’re God’s own child. And because you’re his child, God has given you all the rights of those who are his children.

verses.heading: Paul’s Concern for the Believers in Galatia
verses.subheading: Paul’s Concern for the Believers in Galatia
verses.text: At one time you didn’t know God. You were slaves to gods that aren’t really gods at all.
But now you do know God. Even better, God knows you. So why are you turning back to those weak and worthless powers? Do you want to be slaves to them all over again?
You’re observing special days and months and seasons and years!
I’m afraid for you. I’m concerned that somehow I’ve wasted my efforts on you.
I’m begging you, brothers and sisters: Become like me. After all, I became like you. You didn’t do anything wrong to me.
Remember when I first preached the good news to you? I stopped in your area because I was sick.
I know that my sickness was hard on you. But you weren’t mean to me, and you didn’t make fun of me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God—as if I were Christ Jesus himself.
So why aren’t you treating me the same way now? I know for a fact that if you could have torn out your own eyes and given them to me, you would have.
Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
Those people are trying hard to win you over, but not for your own good. They want to separate from us so that you’ll be eager to follow them.
It’s fine to be eager to do something when it’s for a good purpose. In fact, you should be eager all the time, and not just when I’m with you.
My dear children, once again I’m in pain for you, as if I were a woman giving birth. That’s how much I want to see Christ make you like himself.
I wish I could be with you now and change my tone of voice. I really don’t know what to do with you.

verses.heading: Hagar and Sarah
verses.text: Tell me, you who want to be under the authority of the law: Don’t you know what the law says?
It is written that Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman and the other by a free woman.
Abraham’s son by the slave woman was born in the usual way. But his son by the free woman was born because of a promise from God.
These things are pictures. The two women stand for two covenants. One covenant comes from Mount Sinai, and it gives birth to children who are going to be slaves. That’s Hagar.
Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia. She is like the earthly city of Jerusalem, because she and her children are slaves.
But the heavenly Jerusalem is free, and she is our mother.

It is written, “Be glad, woman, you who have never had children. Shout for joy and cry out loud, you who have never had labor pains. The woman who is all alone has more children than the woman who has a husband.”
Brothers and sisters, you are children who were born as a result of God’s promise, just as Isaac was.
At that time, the son who’d been born in the usual way tried to hurt the other son, who’d been born by the power of the Spirit. It’s the same way now.
But what does Scripture say? “Get rid of the slave woman and her son. The slave woman’s son will never share the family property with the free woman’s son.”
Brothers and sisters, we’re not children of the slave woman. We’re children of the free woman.

verses.heading: Christ Sets Us Free
verses.text: Christ has set us free so that we can be free. So stand firm, and don’t let anyone make you a slave again.
Listen! I, Paul, tell you myself that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ won’t be of any value to you.
I’ll say it again: Every man who lets himself be circumcised must obey the entire law.
Some of you are trying to be made right with God by obeying the law. As a result, you’ve been separated from Christ and you’ve fallen away from God’s grace.
But we, through the Spirit, are eagerly waiting to be made completely right with God by faith.
If a person believes in Christ Jesus, it doesn’t matter whether they’re circumcised or not. The only thing that matters is faith expressing itself through love.
You were running a good race. Who got in your way and kept you from obeying the truth?
Their influence isn’t coming from the God who first called you.
Remember that “a little yeast works its way through the whole batch of dough.”
I’m confident in the Lord that you won’t see this any other way. The people who are getting you so confused will be punished for that, no matter who they are.

Brothers and sisters, if I’m preaching that people have to be circumcised, then why am I getting so much resistance? If I were preaching that, then no one would be offended that they had to trust only in what Jesus did for them on the cross.
As for these troublemakers who are trying to get everybody else circumcised, I wish they’d go the whole way and cut everything off themselves!

verses.heading: Living by the Holy Spirit’s Power
verses.subheading: Living by the Holy Spirit’s Power
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, you were called to be free. But don’t use your freedom as an excuse to live under the power of sin. Instead, serve one another humbly in love.
You can obey the entire law by following this one command: “Love your neighbor as you love yourself.”
But if you say or do things that harm one another, watch out! You could end up destroying one another.
So I say, be guided by the Spirit, and you won’t do what your wrong desires want.
Those desires don’t want what the Spirit wants, and the Spirit doesn’t want what they want. The two are at war with each other, and that’s why you’re not supposed to do whatever you want.
But if you’re guided by the Spirit, then you’re not under the authority of the law.
It’s clear what happens when people follow their wrong desires. There are sexual sins, impure acts, and wild living;
idol-worship and witchcraft; hatred, fighting, jealousy, fits of anger, selfish ambition, arguments, cliques,
and envy; drunkenness, wild parties, and many other things like that. I warn you now, as I did before, that people who live like this won’t inherit God’s kingdom.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, and self-control. There’s no law against things like that.
People who belong to Christ Jesus have nailed their wrong desires to his cross. They don’t want to follow them anymore.
Since we live by the Spirit, let’s keep in step with the Spirit.
Let’s not become proud or make each other angry or want what belongs to someone else.

verses.heading: Do Good to Everyone
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, if someone is caught in a sin, then you who live by the Spirit should correct that person. But do it in a gentle way, and be careful, because you could be tempted too.
Carry one another’s heavy loads, and in that way, you’ll fulfill the law of Christ.
If anyone thinks they’re somebody when they aren’t really anybody, they’re only fooling themselves.
Everyone should test their own actions. Then they’ll be able to take pride in themselves without comparing themselves to others.
In that sense, each person should carry their own load.
But those who are taught the word should share all good things with their teacher.
Don’t get this wrong: You can’t outsmart God. Whatever you plant, that’s what you’re going to harvest.
Some people plant to please their wrong desires, and from those desires they’ll harvest death. Others plant to please the Spirit, and from the Spirit they’ll harvest eternal life.
So let’s not get tired of doing good, because we’ll harvest a crop at the right time if we don’t give up.
So whenever we get the chance to do something good for anyone, let’s do it, and especially for people within the family of believers.

verses.heading: Not Circumcision but the New Creation
verses.subheading: Not Circumcision but the New Creation
verses.text: Look at the big letters I’m using as I write to you with my own hand!
The people who are trying to get you to be circumcised want others to be impressed with them. They don’t want to suffer for saying that we have to depend entirely on the cross of Christ.
Even those who are circumcised don’t follow the law, but they want you to be circumcised so they can brag about getting you to do this.
I don’t ever want to brag about anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through that cross, the world has been crucified to me and I have been crucified to the world.
It doesn’t matter whether a person is circumcised or not. What matters is that the new creation has come.
May peace and mercy be given to all who follow this rule—to the Israel of God.
No one should cause me any more trouble after this, because I have marks on body that show I belong to Jesus.
Brothers and sisters, may the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God. To God’s holy people in Ephesus, who are faithful to Christ Jesus.
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.

verses.heading: Praise God for His Spiritual Blessings in Christ
verses.subheading: Praise God for His Spiritual Blessings in Christ
verses.text: May the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ be praised! He has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing from heaven.
Before the world was created, God chose us in Christ to be holy and blameless in his eyes. Because he loved us,
he chose long ago to adopt us as his children through Jesus Christ. This was what God wanted to do, and it made him happy to do it.
All these things make us want to praise the glorious grace that God has given us freely in the One he loves.
Because Jesus bled and died, our sins have been forgiven, and we’ve been set free. God has poured out his grace
on us so richly! With great wisdom and understanding,
he has shown us the mystery of his will. It expresses his desires and his purposes in Christ.
It will all happen when the time has fully come, when God brings everything in heaven and on earth together under Christ.
God chose us to belong to him, as he had decided long ago in keeping with his plan. He works everything out to fit his plan and purpose.
We were the first to put our hope in Christ, and we were chosen to bring praise to his glory.

You also came to belong to Christ when you heard the message of truth, the good news about how you could be saved. When you believed, God stamped you with an official mark, the Holy Spirit that he promised.
The Spirit is a guarantee that someday we’ll receive all that God has promised. That will happen after God sets all his people completely free. All these things will bring praise to his glory.

verses.heading: Paul Prays and Gives Thanks
verses.text: I’ve heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all of God’s people. That’s why
I haven’t stopped thanking God for you. I always remember you in my prayers.
I keep asking the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, to give you the wisdom and understanding that come from the Holy Spirit. That way you will get to know God better.
I also pray that you may understand more clearly. That way you’ll know the hope that God has called you to, the glorious riches that God will give his holy people,
and the great power of God that’s at work in us as believers. That power can’t be compared with anything else. It’s the same mighty strength
that God showed when he raised Christ from the dead and seated him at his right hand in his heavenly kingdom.
There Christ is far above all rulers and authorities, governors and kings, and every name that people call on, in this world and in the world to come.
God placed all things under Christ’s authority, and he appointed him to be the ruler over everything for the church.
The church is Christ’s body, and he fills it as he fills everything in every way.

verses.heading: God Has Given Us New Life Through Christ
verses.subheading: God Has Given Us New Life Through Christ
verses.text: When you were living in your sins and the wrong things you were doing, you were actually dead.
You were following the ways of this world and serving the one who rules over the spiritual forces of evil. That’s the spirit who’s still at work in those who aren’t obeying God.

At one time we all lived among those things. We followed our wrong desires and thoughts, and we tried to satisfy what they wanted us to do. God was angry with us, as he was with everyone else, because of the kind of people we all were.
But God loves us deeply, and he is full of mercy.
So he gave us new life because of what Christ has done, even when we were dead in our sins. God’s grace has saved you.
God raised us up with Christ and seated us with him in his heavenly kingdom, because we belong to Christ Jesus.
He did that to show for all time the riches of his grace, which can’t be compared with anything else. He demonstrated his grace by being kind to us because of what Christ Jesus has done.
God’s grace has saved you because of your faith in Christ. It’s not from you; it’s God’s gift.
It’s not based on anything you’ve done. No one can brag about earning it.
God made us with his own hands through Christ Jesus for good works, and long ago he prepared them for us as a way of life.

verses.heading: God’s New Family of Jews and Gentiles
verses.subheading: God’s New Family of Jews and Gentiles
verses.text: Some of you are Gentiles, not Jews, by birth. You’re called “uncircumcised” by those who call themselves “circumcised.” But they’ve only been circumcised in their bodies by human hands.

Remember that you used to be separated from Christ. You weren’t considered to be citizens of Israel, and so you didn’t have a share in what the covenants promised. You were without hope and without God in the world.
But now, in Christ Jesus, you who were far away have been brought near to God by the blood of Christ.
Christ himself is our peace. He has brought Jews and Gentiles together into one group of people. He has destroyed the hatred that was like a wall between us.

Through his body on the cross, Christ set aside the law with all its commands and rules. He did this so he could create one new people out of both Jews and Gentiles. He wanted to make peace between them
and bring them back to God as one body. On the cross, Christ put to death the hatred that Jews and Gentiles felt toward one another.
He came and preached peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near.
Through Christ we both come to the Father by one Holy Spirit.
So you’re no longer outsiders and strangers. Instead, you’re citizens together with God’s people, and you’re members of God’s family.
You’re a building that’s being built on the apostles and prophets as its foundation. Christ Jesus himself is the cornerstone that has been laid down first
to make sure all the other stones are properly placed and lined up right. Now the building is rising to become a holy temple.
And because you belong to Christ, you too are being built together to become a place where God can live through his Spirit.

verses.heading: God’s Wonderful Plan for the Gentiles
verses.subheading: God’s Wonderful Plan for the Gentiles
verses.text: I, Paul, am in prison because of my work on behalf of you Gentiles. That’s how I’m serving Christ Jesus.
I’m sure you’ve heard how God gave me a special work to do
by revealing a mystery to me. I’ve written about this just a little.

The mystery is that because of the good news, Gentiles can also receive what God promised to the Jews. Both groups can be part of the same body, and in Christ Jesus, both share in the promise. So by reading this, you’ll be able to recognize the insight I have into the mystery of Christ. It wasn’t made known to people of other times the way the Spirit has now revealed it to God’s holy apostles and prophets.
I became a servant of this good news through the gift of God’s grace. It came through his power, which was at work in me.
I’m less than the least of all the Lord’s people. But he gave me the grace to preach to the Gentiles about the unlimited riches that Christ gives.
God has enabled me to explain to everyone how this mystery has become a reality. In times past it was kept hidden in the mind of God, who created all things.
But now God wants the rulers and authorities in the heavenly world to recognize his great wisdom, and he’s using the church to let them see it.
That was God’s plan from the beginning, and he has fulfilled it through Christ Jesus our Lord.
Through him and through faith in him we can approach God freely and confidently.
So here’s what I’m asking you to do: Don’t be discouraged that I’m suffering for you, because these sufferings are actually an honor for you.

verses.heading: Paul Prays for the Ephesians
verses.text: Because of this I bow in prayer to the Father,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.
I pray that he will use his glorious riches to make you strong with power from his Spirit deep inside of you.
Then Christ will live in your hearts because you believe in him. And I pray that your love will have deep roots and a strong foundation.
May you have power together with all the Lord’s people to understand how wide and long and high and deep Christ’s love is.
And may you know his love, even though it can’t be known completely. Then you will be filled with everything God has for you.
God is able to do far more than we could ever ask for or imagine. He does everything by his power that is at work in us.
So may he receive glory in the church and in Christ Jesus, in every generation, forever and ever! Amen.

verses.heading: Growing Up Together in the Body of Christ
verses.subheading: Growing Up Together in the Body of Christ
verses.text: As a prisoner of the Lord, I ask you to live a life worthy of the purposes God has chosen you to fulfill.
Be completely humble and gentle. Be patient and bear with one another in love.
Do everything you can to stay united in the Spirit and at peace with one another.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called.
There is one Lord, one faith, and one baptism.
There is one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
But each one of us has received the grace that Christ has chosen to give us.
