Demas has deserted me because he’s in love with this world. He has gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia and Titus has gone to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he’s helpful to me in my work for the Lord.
I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the coat that I left with Carpus at Troas. Also bring my scrolls, especially the ones written on parchment.
Alexander the metalworker did a great deal of harm to me. The Lord will pay him back for what he has done.
You should watch out for him too, because he strongly opposed our message.
The first time I was put on trial, no one came to help me. Everyone deserted me. I hope they’ll be forgiven for it.
But the Lord stood at my side and gave me strength, so I was able to preach the message completely, and all the Gentiles heard it. I was saved from the lion’s mouth.
The Lord will save me from every evil attack, and he will bring me safely to his heavenly kingdom. May he receive glory for ever and ever. Amen.

verses.heading: Final Greetings / Final Greetings
verses.text: Greet Priscilla and Aquila and those who live in the house of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
Do your best to get here before winter. Eubulus greets you, and so do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers and sisters.
May the Lord be with your spirit. May God’s grace be with you all.
From Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ. God sent me to help his chosen people deepen their faith and understand even better the truth that leads to godly living.
Then they will live in the hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began that he would give us.
At just the right time, he has revealed this hope through the preaching that he has trusted me to do. God our Savior has commanded all these things.
To Titus, my true son in the faith we share. May God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior give you grace and peace.

verses.heading: Choosing Elders Who Love What Is Good / Choosing Elders Who Love What Is Good
verses.text: I left you on the island of Crete because I wanted you to take care of some unfinished business. I wanted you to appoint elders in every town, and I told you how to do that.
An elder must be blameless. He must be faithful to his wife, and his children must be believers and not give anyone a reason to say that they’re wild and disobedient.
Because a church leader takes care of God’s family, he must be blameless. He must not push people around, or get angry easily, or get drunk, or try to get money by cheating people.
Instead, a church leader must welcome people into his home. He must love what is good and be self-controlled, decent, holy, and disciplined.

He must hold firmly to the trustworthy message as it has been taught. Then he’ll be able to comfort others and build them up with the true teaching, and he’ll be able to prove that people who oppose it are wrong.

verses.heading: Warning People Who Fail to Do Good / Warning People Who Fail to Do Good
verses.text: There are many rebellious people who try to deceive others with smooth talk. This is especially true of those who say that Gentiles who believe in Jesus have to be circumcised.
Those people need to be stopped. They’re disrupting entire families by teaching things they shouldn’t, and they’re doing it just to try to cheat people.
One of Crete’s own prophets has said, “People from Crete are always liars, wild animals, and lazy gluttons.”
That saying is true. I want you to correct these false teachers forcefully, so that they’ll understand the faith properly
and not pay attention to made-up Jewish stories and the merely human commands of people who turn away from the truth.
To people who are pure, all things are pure. But to those who have twisted minds and don’t believe, nothing is pure. Their minds and consciences are corrupted.
They claim that they know God, but their actions show that they don’t know him. They’re despicable, disobedient, and worthless at doing anything good.

verses.heading: Doing Good Because of the Good News / Doing Good Because of the Good News
verses.text: But as for you, teach what agrees with a healthy understanding.
Tell the older men to be restrained, worthy of respect, and self-controlled. Tell them to have genuine faith, love, and endurance.

In the same way, teach the older women to live in a way that shows respect for God. They must not tell lies about others, and they must not become heavy drinkers. Instead, they must teach what is good.
Then they can advise the younger women to love their husbands and children,

to control themselves and be pure, and to take good care of their homes. The younger women must also be taught to be kind and follow the lead of their husbands. Then no one will be able to say bad things about God’s word.
In the same way, encourage the young men to control themselves.
Set an example for them in everything by doing what is good. When you teach, be honest and serious,
and speak in a way that no one can criticize. Then those who oppose you will be embarrassed because they’ll have nothing bad to say about us.
Teach slaves to do everything their masters tell them to do. Tell them to please their masters and not talk back to them.
They must not steal from them, either. Instead, they should show that they can be trusted completely. By doing all these things, they’ll make the teaching about God our Savior very attractive.
The grace of God that offers salvation to all people has now appeared.
It teaches us to say no to godless ways and wrong desires and to live self-controlled, proper, and godly lives in this world
while we wait for Jesus Christ to appear in his glory. That is our blessed hope. Jesus is our great God and Savior.
He gave himself for us to set us free from all wrongdoing and purify us, so that we can be his very own people and be eager to do what is good.
These are the things you should teach. Encourage and correct people with full authority. Don’t let anyone despise you.

verses.heading: Do What Is Good Because You Are Saved / Do What Is Good Because You Are Saved
verses.text: Remind God’s people to follow their rulers and authorities and to be ready to do what is good.
Tell them not to say bad things about anybody but to live in peace, consider the needs of others, and always be gentle toward everyone.
At one time we too were foolish, disobedient, deceived, and controlled by all kinds of wrong desires and pleasures. We were hostile and envious. Other people hated us, and we hated them.
But when the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared,
he saved us, not because of any good things we had done, but because of his mercy. He saved us by washing away our sins so that we were born again.
God poured out the Spirit on us generously through Jesus Christ our Savior, and the Spirit gave us new life.
Now, because God has made us right with himself by his grace, we have the hope of inheriting eternal life.

This is a saying you can trust. I want you to emphasize these things so that those who trust in God will be careful to commit themselves to doing good. These things are excellent and good for everyone.
But stay away from foolish disagreements, long ancestry lists, arguments, and fights about what the law teaches. None of those things do any good or help anybody.
If someone is causing divisions, warn them once, and then warn them again if you have to, but after that, don’t have anything to do with them.
You know that people like that warp themselves and keep sinning. Their own actions show how wrong they are.

verses.heading: Final Words / Final Words
verses.text: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis. I’ve decided to spend the winter there.
Do everything you can to help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos. Send them on their way and make sure they have everything they need.
Our people must learn to devote themselves to doing what is good. Then they’ll be able to take care of people who have urgent needs, and they won’t be living useless lives.
Everyone with me sends you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. May God’s grace be with you all.
From Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother. To Philemon, our dear friend who works together with us;
our sister Apphia; Archippus, who is a soldier of Christ together with us; and the church that meets in your home.
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.

verses.heading: Paul Prays and Gives Thanks / Paul Prays and Gives Thanks
verses.text: I always thank my God when I remember you in my prayers.
I’ve heard about your love for all God’s people and your faith in the Lord Jesus.
I pray that the faith we have in common will help you understand even better every good thing that we share for the sake of Christ.
Your love has given me great joy and encouragement, because you, my brother, have refreshed the hearts of the Lord’s people.

verses.heading: Paul Makes an Appeal for Onesimus / Paul Makes an Appeal for Onesimus
verses.text: Because of the authority Christ has given me, I could be bold and order you to do what you should do.
But I would rather appeal to you on the basis of love. I, Paul, am an old man, and now I’m also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
Simply as that person, I want to appeal to you on behalf of my son Onesimus. He became a son to me while I was being held in chains.
Before that, he was useless to you, but now he has become useful to you and to me.
I’m sending Onesimus back to you, even though that’s like sending away my own heart.
I would have liked to keep Onesimus with me so he could take your place in helping me while I’m being held in chains because of the good news I am offering.
But I didn’t want to do anything without your agreement. Any favor you do for me must be done because you want to do it, not because you have to. Maybe
Onesimus was separated from you for a little while so you could have him back forever,

not as a slave anymore, but as something much better than a slave. He is a dear brother to me but even more so to you, because now he will be not just a member of your household but also your brother in the Lord.
If you consider me your partner in God’s work, then accept Onesimus as you would accept me.
If he has done anything wrong to you, or if he owes you anything, then charge it to me.
I, Paul, am writing this pledge with my own hand: I will pay it back. I won’t even mention that you owe me your very self.
I wish, my brother, to receive some benefit from you in the Lord. So please refresh my heart in Christ.
I’m confident that you will obey, and so I’m writing to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
There’s one more thing: Have a guest room ready for me. I hope that I’ll be released and that I’ll be able to come see you, in answer to your prayers.
Epaphras, who’s a prisoner with me in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings.
Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who work together with me, also send you greetings.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

verses.heading: God Speaks His Final Word Through His Son / God Speaks His Final Word Through His Son
verses.text: In the past, God spoke to our people a little at a time in different ways through the prophets.
But in these last days, he has spoken to us through his Son. God made the universe through him and gave him everything as his inheritance.

The Son is the brilliance of God’s glory and the exact likeness of God’s being. He holds everything together by his powerful word. Once he had provided the way for people to be made pure from sin, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty in heaven.
This made him higher than the angels, just as much as the name he has received is superior to theirs.

verses.heading: The Son Is Greater Than the Angels / The Son Is Greater Than the Angels
verses.text: After all, God never said to any of the angels, “You are my Son, today I have become your Father.” Or, “I will be his Father, and he will be my Son.”
Again, when God brings his firstborn into the world, he says, “Let all God’s angels worship him.”
God also says this about the angels: “God makes his angels spirits and his servants flames of fire.”
But about the Son he says, “God, your throne will last for ever and ever. You will rule your kingdom with justice and righteousness.
You have loved what is right and hated what is wrong, so your God has placed you above your companions and poured the sacred oil of joy on your head.”
He also says, “Lord, in the beginning you placed the earth on its foundations, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will pass away, but you will remain. They will all wear out like a piece of clothing.
You’ll roll them up like a robe; they’ll be changed like clothes. But you’ll remain the same, and your years will never end.”
God never said to an angel, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your control.”
Aren’t all the angels spirits that God sends to serve those who will inherit salvation?

verses.heading: A Warning to Pay Attention / A Warning to Pay Attention
verses.text: So we must pay very careful attention to what we’ve heard, so that we don’t drift away from it.
The message that God spoke through the angels had to be obeyed. Every time people broke the Law or didn’t obey God, they were punished.
So then how will we escape if we don’t pay attention to the even greater salvation that the Lord Jesus announced? Those who heard him told us what he said,
and then God showed that their report was true by doing signs and wonders and various kinds of miracles and by giving out gifts from the Holy Spirit as he wished.

verses.heading: Jesus Was Made Fully Human / Jesus Was Made Fully Human
verses.text: God hasn’t put angels in charge of the world that’s going to come, which we’ve been talking about.
There’s a place in Scripture where someone has said, “What are human beings that you should be concerned about them? What is a son of man that you take care of him?
But you made them a little lower than the angels, you crowned them with glory and honor,
and you put everything under their control.” When God put everything under their control, he didn’t leave anything out of their control. Everything isn’t under their control just yet.

But we can see that Jesus has already been crowned with glory and honor because he suffered and died. He was made lower than the angels for a little while so that by the grace of God he could taste death for everyone.

God, who made everything, wanted his many sons and daughters to share in his glory. He chose Jesus to be the one to lead them into their salvation, and he made him perfect through suffering so he could accomplish that.
Jesus, who makes people holy, belongs to the same family as the people he makes holy. That’s why he isn’t ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters.
He says, “I’ll announce your name to my brothers and sisters. I’ll sing your praises among those who worship you.”
Again he says, “I will put my trust in him.” He also says, “Here I am, and here are the children God has given me.”

Because those children have bodies made out of flesh and blood, Jesus became human like them in order to die for them. By doing that, he could stop the one who rules over the kingdom of death, that is, the devil,
and set free people who were held as slaves all their lives by the fear of death.
It’s certainly not angels that he helps, but Abraham’s children.
So he had to be made like them—fully human in every way. That way he could serve God as a merciful and faithful high priest and purify the people from their sins.
Because he himself suffered when he was tempted, he’s able to help others who are being tempted.

verses.heading: Jesus Is Greater Than Moses / Jesus Is Greater Than Moses
verses.text: Holy brothers and sisters, who take part in God’s calling, I want you to focus your attention on Jesus, who is the messenger and high priest of our faith.
Jesus was faithful to the one who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in God’s whole house.
But Jesus has been found worthy of greater honor than Moses, just as the person who builds a house is honored more than the house itself.
Every house is built by someone, but God has built everything.
“Moses was faithful as a servant in God’s whole house.” He was a witness to what God would say in the future.
But Christ is faithful over God’s house as his Son. And we are his house, if we hold tightly to our courage and the hope we boast about.

verses.heading: A Warning Against Unbelief / A Warning Against Unbelief
verses.text: The Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear his voice,
don’t be stubborn, the way you were when you rebelled against me in the time of testing in the desert.
There your people of long ago tested me, even though for 40 years they saw what I did.
That’s why I was angry with them and said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, they haven’t known my ways.’
So when I was angry, I swore an oath: ‘They’ll never enter the rest I planned for them.’ ”
Brothers and sisters, make sure that none of you has a sinful, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, while it’s still called “Today,” so that sin doesn’t deceive any of you and harden you.
We have come to share in Christ, but we need to maintain right to the end the confidence we started with.
As it has just been said, “Today, if you hear his voice, don’t be stubborn, the way you were when you rebelled against me.”
Who were those who heard but rebelled? Weren’t they all the people that Moses led out of Egypt?
Who was God angry with for 40 years? Wasn’t he angry with those who sinned, who died in the desert?
And who did God swear an oath about, that they would never enter the rest he planned for them? Didn’t he swear that oath about the people who didn’t obey?
So we see that because they didn’t believe, they weren’t able to enter.

verses.heading: God’s People Enter His Sabbath Rest / God’s People Enter His Sabbath Rest
verses.text: But the promise of entering God’s rest is still open. So I want you all to be careful not to miss it.
The good news has been preached to us, just as it was to our people of long ago. But the message they heard didn’t do them any good, because they didn’t embrace it by faith when they heard it.

But we do have faith, and we can still enter that rest. God said, “When I was angry, I swore an oath: ‘They’ll never enter the rest I planned for them.’ ” God said that even though he’d already been resting ever since he finished creating the world.
Somewhere in Scripture he has spoken about the seventh day this way: “On the seventh day God rested from all his works.”
But in the passage just quoted, God said, “They’ll never enter the rest I planned for them.”
So some people can still enter that rest. Those who had the good news announced to them earlier didn’t obey, and so they didn’t go in.
So God chose another day, calling it “Today,” when he spoke through David a long time later, in the passage we’ve been considering: “Today, if you hear his voice, don’t be stubborn.”
It’s true that Joshua led the next generation of Israelites into the promised land. But if that had been the rest God said he was planning, God wouldn’t have spoken later about another day.
So there must still be a Sabbath rest available for God’s people.
Anyone who enters God’s rest also rests from their own work, just as God rested from his.
So let’s make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will die by disobeying the way the people of long ago did.

The word of God is alive and active. It’s even sharper than any sword that has two edges. It penetrates deep inside us, to where the bones meet the joints and where the soul meets the spirit, until it reveals the thoughts and intentions of our hearts.
Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight. His eyes see everything, and he’ll hold us accountable for everything we do.

verses.heading: Jesus Is the Great High Priest / Jesus Is the Great High Priest
verses.text: Because we have a great high priest who has gone up into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let’s hold on firmly to our faith.
We don’t have a high priest who can’t feel what we feel when we’re weak. Instead, we have a high priest who has been tempted in every way just as we are, but without sinning.
So let’s approach God’s throne of grace confidently, because we’ll receive mercy there and find grace to help us in our time of need.
Every high priest is chosen from among the people and appointed to represent them in things relating to God. He offers gifts and sacrifices for their sins.
He’s able to deal gently with people who don’t realize what they’re doing and go astray, because he himself is weak.
That’s why he has to offer sacrifices for his own sins as well as for the sins of the people.
And no one can claim this honor for himself; instead, he receives it when he’s called by God, just as Aaron was.
In the same way, Christ didn’t claim for himself the privilege of becoming a high priest. But God said to him, “You are my Son, today I have become your Father.”
In another place God said, “You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek.”
During the days of Jesus’ life on earth, with loud cries and tears he prayed to and pleaded with the God who could save him from death, and God listened to him because of his reverence.
Even though Jesus was God’s Son, he learned through suffering what it means to obey.
Once he had been made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey him.
God appointed him to be a high priest in the order of Melchizedek.

verses.heading: A Warning Against Falling Away / A Warning Against Falling Away
verses.text: We have a lot to say about this, but it’s hard to make it clear to you because you no longer try to understand.
By this time, you should be teachers, but instead you need someone to teach you the basic truths of God’s word all over again. You need milk, not solid food.
Anyone who lives on milk is still a baby. That person doesn’t know how to live a godly life.
Solid food is for people who have grown up, who have trained themselves to know the difference between good and evil.

So let’s move on beyond the basic teachings about Christ and grow up as believers. Let’s not start all over from the beginning. We already know that we need to turn away from doing things that lead to death. We know that we must have faith in God.
We’ve learned about different ways of becoming clean and about placing hands on people to bless them. We know that people will rise from the dead and that God will judge everyone for eternity.
So now I want to talk about things beyond these basic teachings, and I’ll do that as God allows.
If a person falls away from the faith after seeing the light, tasting the gift from heaven, sharing in the Holy Spirit,
and tasting the good things of God’s word and the powers of the coming age,

it’s not possible to bring them back. They won’t be able to turn away from their sins. They’re nailing the Son of God to the cross all over again and bringing shame on him in front of everyone—although they’re the ones who are really losing out.
God blesses any land that soaks up rain and produces a crop useful to the farmer.
But land that produces only thorns and weeds isn’t worth anything. It’s in danger of coming under God’s curse. In the end, it will be burned.
Even though we’re talking like this, we’re sure of better things in your case, dear friends—things that go with being saved.
God isn’t unfair. He won’t forget what you’ve done and the love you’ve shown him as you’ve helped his people and as you keep on helping them.
We want each of you to show this same dedication to the very end, so that everything you’re hoping for will happen.
We don’t want you to become lazy. Instead, imitate those who receive through faith and patience what God has promised.

verses.heading: God Keeps His Promise / God Keeps His Promise
verses.text: When God made his promise to Abraham, he swore an oath by himself—there was no one greater to swear an oath by.
He said, “I will certainly bless you and give you many children.”
Abraham waited patiently, and then he received what God had promised him.

People swear an oath by someone who’s greater than they are, and the oath guarantees that they’ll keep their promise. After that, nobody argues about whether the person really meant what they were saying.
When God made his promise to Abraham and his family, he wanted them to know that he’d never change his mind.

That’s why he swore an oath. Then there were two things that guaranteed God was telling the truth: his promise and his oath. He gave us those two things so that we’d be very encouraged as we run to take hold of the hope that has been set before us.
It’s like a firm and secure anchor for our souls. This hope leads all the way into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain,
where Jesus has gone to open the way ahead of us. He has become a high priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek.

verses.heading: Melchizedek the Priest / Melchizedek the Priest
verses.text: This Melchizedek was the king of Salem and a priest of God Most High. When Abraham was coming back from winning a battle against a group of kings, Melchizedek met him and blessed him.
Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he’d captured in the battle. First, the name Melchizedek means “king of what is right.” Then, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”
Melchizedek has no father or mother or family line. His life has no beginning or ending. He remains a priest forever, like the Son of God.
Think how great Melchizedek was! Even our father Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had captured.

Now the law says that the sons of Levi who become priests must collect a tenth from all the people. They collect it from the other Israelites even though they all belong to the family line of Abraham.
Melchizedek didn’t trace his family line from Levi, but he still collected a tenth from Abraham. Melchizedek blessed the one who had received the promises.
There’s no question that the more important person blesses the less important one.
In the case of the Levites, the tenth is received by people who eventually die. But in the case of Melchizedek, it’s received by someone who’s said to be living.
We might even say that Levi, who receives the tenth from the Israelites, paid it to Melchizedek through Abraham,
because when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in Abraham’s body.

verses.heading: Jesus Is Like Melchizedek / Jesus Is Like Melchizedek
verses.text: If the priests who came from Levi’s family could have made the people perfect by what they did at the temple, then why would another priest have to come who wasn’t in the order of Aaron, but in the order of Melchizedek? The law that was given to the people said that priests had to come from Levi’s family line.
So if the priests are changed, then the law must be changed too.
God said these things about Jesus, and he was from a different tribe. No one from his tribe has ever served at the altar.
It’s clear that our Lord came from the family line of Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests coming from that tribe.
What we’re saying becomes even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,
someone who has become a priest not because of a rule about his family line but because of the power of a life that can never be destroyed.
Scripture says, “You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek.”
The old rule is set aside because it was weak and useless.
The law didn’t make anything perfect, but a better hope has now been given to us, and it brings us near to God.
Notice that God changed the priests by swearing an oath. The ones from Levi’s family line became priests without God swearing an oath.
But when Jesus became a priest, God confirmed this with an oath when he said to him, “The Lord has sworn an oath and he won’t change his mind. He has said, ‘You are a priest forever.’ ”
Because of this oath, Jesus guarantees that we have a better covenant with God.
There had to be many priests in Levi’s family line, because the old ones died, and new ones were needed to replace them.
But Jesus lives forever, so he never stops being a priest.
That’s why he’s able to save completely and for all time people who come to God through him. Jesus never stops praying for them.
A high priest like him truly meets our needs. He’s holy, blameless, and pure, and he has been lifted up high above the heavens. He’s different from people who sin.

Unlike the other high priests, he doesn’t need to offer sacrifices day after day, first for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. Instead, Jesus made one sacrifice for the sins of the people, once and for all time, when he offered himself.
The law appoints men who are weak to be high priests. But after the law had been given, God swore an oath and appointed his Son, who has been made perfect forever.

verses.heading: The High Priest of a New Covenant / The High Priest of a New Covenant
verses.text: Here’s the main point of what we’re saying: We have just this kind of high priest, who’s sitting at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven.
Now he serves in the heavenly sanctuary, the true holy tent set up by the Lord, not by mere human beings.
Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices, so this priest had to have something to offer too.
If he were on earth, he wouldn’t be a priest, because there already are priests who offer the gifts required by the law.

They serve at a sanctuary that’s a picture and shadow of what’s in heaven. That’s why God warned Moses when he was about to build the holy tent, “When you make everything, be sure to follow the pattern I showed you on the mountain.”

But Jesus has been given a greater work to do for God. He’s the mediator of a new covenant. It’s better than the old one, because it’s based on better promises. Jesus’ work is greater than the work of the earthly priests, just as much as the new covenant is better than the old one.
If nothing had been wrong with that first covenant, no one would have tried to make room for another covenant.
But God did find something wrong with the people. He said, “The days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and with the people of Judah.

It won’t be like the covenant I made with their people of long ago when I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt, because they didn’t remain faithful to my covenant, and I turned away from them, says the Lord.

This is the covenant I will establish with the people of Israel after that time, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
They won’t teach their neighbor anymore, and one person won’t say to one another, ‘Know the Lord.’ That’s because everyone will know me, from the least of them to the greatest.
I will forgive their evil ways and I won’t remember their sins anymore.”
By calling this covenant “new,” God made the first one outdated. And what is outdated and obsolete will soon disappear.

verses.heading: Worship in the Holy Tent on Earth / Worship in the Holy Tent on Earth
verses.text: The first covenant had rules for worship, and it also had an earthly sanctuary.
A holy tent was set up. The first room in it had the lampstand and the table with the holy bread. This was called the Holy Place.
Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place.

It had the golden altar for incense and the wooden chest called the ark of the covenant. The ark was covered with gold. It held the gold jar of manna, Aaron’s walking stick that had budded, and the stone tablets that had the words of the covenant written on them.
Above the ark, where God showed his glory, there were cherubim made of gold. They spread their wings over the place where sin was paid for. But we can’t discuss these things in detail now.
That’s how everything was arranged in the holy tent. The priests came regularly into the outer room to do their work.

But only the high priest could go into the inner room, and he could only go in once a year. He never entered without bringing blood with him, which he had to offer for himself and for the sins the people had committed without knowing any better.
The Holy Spirit was showing us that God had not yet opened the way into the Most Holy Place as long as the first tent was there.
It’s an illustration of the present time, when gifts and sacrifices are offered that can’t give the worshiper a clear conscience.
They deal only with food and drink and different kinds of ceremonial washings, which are rules about the outside of a person. They had to be followed only until the new covenant came.

verses.heading: The Blood of Christ / The Blood of Christ
verses.text: But then, when Christ came as the high priest of the good things that have already arrived, he went through the greater and more perfect holy tent. That tent wasn’t made with human hands. In other words, it’s not part of this creation.

He didn’t enter by shedding the blood of goats and calves. Instead, he entered the Most Holy Place by shedding his own blood, once and for all time. In that way, he paid the price to set us free from sin forever.
The blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a young cow are sprinkled on people the law calls unclean in order to make them holy. Then they’re considered clean on the outside.

So how much cleaner will the blood of Christ make us! He offered himself to God without any flaw through the power of the eternal Holy Spirit. His blood washes away our feelings of guilt for committing sin. Sin always leads to death. But now we can serve the living God.

That’s why Christ is the mediator of a new covenant. Now the people that God has called to himself can receive the eternal gift he promised. They can receive it because Christ has died to pay the price and set them free from the sins they committed under the first covenant.
When someone leaves a will, it’s necessary to prove that the person who made it has died,
because someone’s will only takes effect when they die. It never takes effect while the person who made it is still living.
That’s why even the first covenant was not put into effect without the shedding of blood.

Moses first announced every command of the law to all the people. Then he took the blood of calves, together with water, bright red wool, and branches from a hyssop plant, and he sprinkled the Book of the Covenant and all the people.
He said, “This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded you to keep.”
In the same way, he sprinkled the holy tent and everything used in worship there with blood.
In fact, the law requires that nearly everything be made clean with blood. Without the shedding of blood, there is no forgiveness of sin.
So the copies of the heavenly things had to be made pure with these sacrifices. But the heavenly things themselves had to be made pure with better sacrifices.
Christ didn’t enter a sanctuary made with human hands that was only a copy of the true one. He entered heaven itself in order to appear before God on our behalf. He’s there right now.
The high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that isn’t his own. But Christ didn’t enter heaven to offer himself again and again.

If he had, he would have had to suffer many times since the world was created. No, he has appeared once and for all time, now when God’s work is being completed. He has come to do away with sin by offering himself.
People have to die once, and after that they face judgment.

In the same way, Christ was sacrificed once to take away the sins of many people. He will also come a second time, not to take away our sins, but to bring salvation to those who are eagerly waiting for him.

verses.heading: Christ’s Sacrifice Is Once and for All Time / Christ’s Sacrifice Is Once and for All Time
verses.text: The law is only a shadow of the good things that are coming. It’s not the real things themselves. That’s why the law can never, through the same sacrifices that are repeated endlessly year after year, make perfect the people who come near to worship.
If it could, wouldn’t those sacrifices have stopped being offered? The worshipers would have been made clean once and for all time. They wouldn’t feel guilty for their sins anymore.
But those offerings remind people of their sins every year,
because it’s impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
That’s why Christ said, when he came into the world, “You didn’t want sacrifices and offerings. Instead, you prepared a body for me.
You weren’t pleased with burnt offerings and sin offerings.
Then I said, ‘Here I am. As it’s written about me in the book, I’ve come to do your will, my God.’ ”

First he said, “You didn’t want sacrifices and offerings, and you weren’t pleased with burnt offerings and sin offerings.” He said this even though these things were being offered as the law required.
Then he said, “Here I am, I’ve come to do your will.” He sets aside the sacrifices and offerings in favor of the will of God.
And by that will, we’ve been made holy through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once and for all time.
Day after day every priest stands and performs his special duties. He offers the same sacrifices again and again, even though they can’t ever take away sins.
But when Jesus, our priest, had offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, he sat down at the right hand of God.
Since that time, he’s been waiting for his enemies to be put under his control.
By that one sacrifice he has made perfect forever those who are being made holy.
The Holy Spirit also speaks to us about this. First he says,
“This is the covenant I will establish with the people of Israel after that time, says the Lord. I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts.”
Then he adds, “I will forget their evil ways, and I won’t remember their sins anymore.”
And where these sins have been forgiven, a sacrifice for sin is no longer necessary.

verses.heading: An Appeal and Warning to Remain Faithful / An Appeal and Warning to Remain Faithful
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, we have the confidence to enter the Most Holy Place because of the blood of Jesus.
He has opened a new and life-giving way for us through the curtain, that is, his body.
We also have a great priest over the house of God.

So let’s draw near to God with a sincere heart and with the full assurance that faith brings. Our hearts have been sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience, and our bodies have been washed with pure water.
Let’s hold firmly to the hope we say we have, because the one who promised is faithful.
And let’s consider how we can stir one another up to love and good works.

Let’s not give up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing. Instead, let’s encourage one another. And let’s meet and encourage one another even more as we see the day of Christ’s return approaching.
If we deliberately keep on sinning after we’ve come to know the truth, then there’s no offering left for our sins.
All we can do is to wait in fear for God’s punishment and the blazing fire that will burn up his enemies.
If anyone broke the law of Moses, that person would die without mercy if two or three witnesses gave evidence against them.
But wouldn’t people deserve even more punishment if they’ve trampled the Son of God under their feet, treated the blood of the covenant as unholy, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
We know the God who said, “I’m the God who judges people, and I will pay them back.” Scripture also says, “The Lord will judge his people.”
It’s a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Remember those earlier days after you received the light. You remained strong in a great struggle even though you suffered greatly.
Sometimes people spoke badly about you in front of others. Sometimes you were mistreated. At other times you stood side by side with people who were being treated like that.
You suffered along with people in prison, and when your property was taken from you, you accepted that with joy, because you knew that God had given you better and more lasting things.
So don’t throw away your confidence. It will be richly rewarded.
You need to stand firm so that when you’ve done God’s will, you’ll receive what he has promised.
“In just a little while, he who is coming will come. He won’t wait any longer.”
And, “The one who’s right with God will live by faith. But I’m not pleased with the one who pulls back.”
We’re not among the people who pull back and are destroyed. We’re among the people who have faith and are saved.

verses.heading: Faith That Produces Action / Faith That Produces Action
verses.text: Faith is having confidence in what we hope for and being sure of what we don’t see.
That’s what the people of long ago were praised for.
By faith we understand that everything was made at God’s command, so that what we see was made out of what was not visible.

By faith Abel brought a better offering to God than Cain did. Because of his faith, Abel was praised as a godly man when God said good things about his offerings. And by faith Abel still speaks, even though he has died.

By faith Enoch was taken from this life so that he didn’t experience death. “He couldn’t be found, because God had taken him away.” Before God took him, Enoch was praised as someone who had pleased God.
Without faith it’s impossible to please God, because those who come to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who try hard to find him.

By faith Noah, out of great respect for God, built an ark to save his family after God warned him about things that could not yet be seen. By doing this Noah showed the world that it was guilty, but he was considered right with God because of his faith.
By faith Abraham obeyed God and went to the place he would later receive as his own. He did that even though he didn’t know where he was going when God told him to start on his way there.
By faith he made his home in the promised land like an outsider in a strange country. He lived there in tents, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who received the same promise he did.
Abraham was looking forward to the city that has foundations, the one that God has planned and built.
By faith Sarah was able to become a mother even when she was too old to have children. God had promised this would happen, and Sarah believed that he was faithful.
Abraham was also past the time when he could have children, but from that one man came as many children as the stars in the sky and the countless grains of sand on the seashore.

All of these people were still living by faith when they died. They didn’t receive the things God had promised; they only saw them and welcomed them from a long way off. They admitted that they were outsiders and strangers on earth.
People who say things like that show that they’re looking for a country of their own.
If they’d been thinking of the country they left, they would have had a chance to return there.
Instead, they were longing for a better country, a heavenly one. So God isn’t ashamed to be called their God, because he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham offered Isaac as a sacrifice when God tested him. This man who had welcomed the promises was ready to offer his one and only son.
God had said to him, “Your family line will continue through Isaac.” Even so, Abraham was ready to offer him up.
Abraham did this because he believed that God could bring back people who had died. And so, in a sense, he did receive Isaac back from the dead.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau and told them what was going to happen to them.
By faith Jacob blessed both of Joseph’s sons when he was dying. He worshiped God as he leaned on the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph spoke to the people of Israel about how they would leave Egypt someday. As he was dying, he told them to take his bones with them, to be buried back in their land.
By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after he was born. They saw that he was a special child, and they weren’t afraid of the king’s command.
By faith Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter after he had grown up.
He chose to be treated badly with God’s people rather than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a short time.
He considered it more valuable to suffer shame for Christ than to have the riches of Egypt, because he was looking ahead to his reward.
By faith Moses left Egypt. He knew this would make Pharaoh angry, but he wasn’t afraid. He didn’t let anything stop him, because he saw the God who can’t be seen.
By faith Moses kept the Passover Feast. He commanded the people of Israel to sprinkle blood on their doorways so that the destroying angel wouldn’t kill their oldest sons.
By faith the people of Israel passed through the Red Sea as if it were dry land, but when the Egyptians tried to do that, they were drowned.
By faith Israel’s army marched around the city of Jericho for seven days, and then its walls fell down.
By faith Rahab, the prostitute, welcomed the spies, and she wasn’t killed with those who didn’t obey God.
What more can I say? I don’t have time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, and Jephthah, or about David and Samuel and the prophets.
By faith they conquered kingdoms, ruled fairly, and received the blessings God had promised. They shut the mouths of lions,
put out great fires, and escaped being killed by swords. Their weakness was turned to strength, they became powerful in battle, and they beat back armies from other countries.

Women received their loved ones back when they were raised from the dead. Others had to suffer greatly, but they refused to be set free, so that after death they could be raised to an even better life.
Some were insulted and whipped; some were held in chains and put in prison.
Some were killed with stones, some were sawed in two, and some were killed by swords. They went around wearing the skins of sheep and goats. They were poor, systematically oppressed, and mistreated.
They wandered in deserts and mountains, and they lived in caves and holes in the ground. The world was not worthy of them.
All these people were honored for their faith, but none of them received what God had promised.
That’s because God had planned something better for us. God wanted to make them perfect only when he could make us perfect with them.
Since we’re surrounded by such a huge cloud of witnesses, let’s throw off everything that weighs us down and any sin that gets in our way. Let’s keep on running the race on the course in front of us.

And let’s keep looking to Jesus. He’s the one who leads us into faith and the one who makes our faith mature. Because of the joy he was looking forward to, he didn’t let the shame of being put to death on a cross stop him. He suffered on the cross, and then he sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Think about how he endured such opposition from sinners, so that you don’t get worn out and give up.

verses.heading: God Trains His Children / God Trains His Children
verses.text: In your own struggle against sin, you haven’t yet resisted to the point where your blood has been shed.

Don’t forget this word of encouragement that speaks to you the way a father speaks to his children: “My son, don’t think the Lord’s discipline doesn’t matter, and don’t give up hope when he corrects you,
because the Lord disciplines the one he loves and he corrects everyone he accepts as his son.”
So stay strong during hard times, because God is using them to train you. He’s treating you as his own children. That’s what parents do—they discipline their children.
If God doesn’t discipline you, then you’re not God’s genuine sons and daughters at all.
Besides, we’ve all had human fathers who disciplined us, and we obeyed them. So we should certainly obey the Father of spirits and benefit from his correction.
Our parents disciplined us for a short time as they thought best. But God disciplines us for our good so that we can share in his holiness.
No discipline seems pleasant at the time. Instead, it seems painful. But later on it produces a harvest of godliness and peace for those who have been trained by it.
So if your hands are weak, make them strong. If your legs won’t hold you up, then strengthen them too.
“Make level paths for your feet to walk on.” Then those who have trouble walking will be healed, and they won’t have difficulty anymore.

verses.heading: A Warning and an Appeal / A Warning and an Appeal
verses.text: Try your best to live at peace with everyone. Do everything you can to be holy, because without holiness no one will see the Lord.
Make sure that no one misses out on God’s grace and that no bitter plant grows up, because if it does, it will cause trouble and make many people impure.
And make sure that no one is sexually immoral or godless like Esau, who sold his rights as the oldest son for a single meal.
As you know, afterwards he wanted to receive his father’s blessing, but he was turned away. Even though he pleaded with tears, he still couldn’t change what he had done.

verses.heading: The Mountain of Fear and the Mountain of Joy / The Mountain of Fear and the Mountain of Joy
verses.text: You haven’t come to a mountain that could be touched and that’s burning with fire. You haven’t come to darkness, gloom, and storm,
or to a loud trumpet blast, or to the voice of God speaking to you. When the Israelites heard that voice long ago, they begged it not to say anything more to them.
They were too scared by the command, “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be killed with stones.”
The sight was so terrifying that Moses said, “I’m shaking with fear.”
No, you’ve come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You’ve come to a place where thousands and thousands of angels have gathered to celebrate.

You’ve come to a special community of people: God considers each and every one of them to be his firstborn child! Their names are written in heaven. You’ve come to God, the Judge of all, and to the spirits of godly people who’ve been made perfect.
You’ve come to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks better things than the blood of Abel, which cried out from the ground for revenge.

So make sure that you don’t disobey the one who’s speaking to you now. If they didn’t escape when they disobeyed the one who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we disobey the one who’s warning us from heaven!
At that time his voice shook the earth, but now he has promised, “I’m going to shake the earth once more, and when I do, I’m also going to shake the heavens.”
The words “once more” show that the things that can be shaken (that is, created things) are going to be taken away. Then the things that can’t be shaken will remain.
Since we’re receiving a kingdom that can’t be shaken, let’s be thankful, and let’s worship God in a way that pleases him. Let’s worship him with deep respect and wonder,
because our “God is like a fire that burns everything up.”

verses.heading: Final Appeals / Final Appeals
verses.text: Keep on loving one another as brothers and sisters.
Don’t forget to welcome strangers. By doing that, some people have welcomed angels without knowing it.
Keep on remembering those in prison as if you were together with them in prison, and continue to remember those who are being treated badly as if you yourselves were suffering.
Marriage should be honored by everyone and the marriage bed should be kept pure. God will judge anyone who commits adultery or any other sexual sin.
Keep your lives free from the love of money, and be content with what you have, because God has said, “I’ll never leave you; I’ll never abandon you.”
So we can confidently say, “The Lord is my helper; I won’t be afraid. What can mere human beings do to me?”
Remember your leaders, who spoke God’s word to you. Think about the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

Don’t be led astray by all kinds of strange teachings. It’s good for our hearts to be made strong by God’s grace, not by eating foods that the law requires. Those foods don’t do anything for the people who eat them.
We have an altar that those who serve in the holy tent have no right to eat from.
The high priest carries the blood of animals into the Most Holy Place as a sin offering, but their bodies are burned outside the camp.
Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to make the people holy by shedding his own blood.
So let’s go to him outside the camp and be willing to suffer the shame he suffered.
We don’t have a lasting city here. Instead, we’re looking for the city that’s going to come.
Let’s keep talking openly about our faith in Jesus. Then our words will be like a sacrifice to God, offered through Jesus.
Don’t forget to do good and share with others, because God is pleased with offerings like those.

Have confidence in your leaders and put yourselves under their authority, because they’re keeping watch over you as people who will have to answer to God for everything they do. Do this so that their work will be a joy, not a burden. It wouldn’t help you at all if you made their work more difficult.
Pray for us. We’re sure that we’ve done what’s right, but we want to keep on living honorably in every way.
I particularly ask you to pray that I’ll be able to come back to you soon.

verses.heading: Final Blessing and Greetings / Final Blessing and Greetings
verses.text: Our Lord Jesus is the great Shepherd of the sheep. The God of peace brought him back from the dead through the blood of the eternal covenant. May that same God
supply you with everything good so that you can do his will. May he create in us what is pleasing to him through Jesus Christ. And may Jesus receive glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I ask you, brothers and sisters, to listen carefully to the challenges and encouragement that I’ve offered you briefly.
I want you to know that our brother Timothy has been set free. If he arrives here soon, I’ll come with him to see you.
Greet all your leaders and all the Lord’s people. The believers from Italy send you their greetings.
May God’s grace be with all of you.
From James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ. To the 12 tribes scattered among the nations. Greetings.

verses.heading: Facing All Kinds of Trouble / Facing All Kinds of Trouble
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, think of it as pure joy when you face all kinds of trouble.
When your faith is tested, this develops endurance in you.
You must allow endurance to finish its work so that you’ll be everything you should be and have everything you need.
If any of you needs wisdom, you should ask God for it, and he’ll give it to you. God gives freely to everyone and doesn’t tell them they shouldn’t have asked.
But when you ask, you must believe and not doubt, because a person who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed around by the wind.
That kind of person shouldn’t expect to receive anything from the Lord.
They can’t make up their mind and they can never decide what to do.
Believers who are in low positions in life should be proud that God has given them a high position in the kingdom.
But rich people should take pride in their low positions, since they will fade away like wild flowers.
The sun rises, and its burning heat dries up the plants. Their blossoms fall and their beauty is destroyed. In the same way, rich people will fade away even as they go about their business.
Blessed is the person who keeps going when times are difficult. After they’ve made it through these times, they’ll receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to give to those who love him.
When a person is tempted, they shouldn’t say, “God is tempting me.” God can’t be tempted by evil, and he doesn’t tempt anyone.
Instead, each person is tempted by their own evil desires, which lead them on and drag them away.
These desires have a child known as sin, and when sin grows up, it leads to death.
Don’t let anyone fool you, my dear brothers and sisters.
Every good and perfect gift is from above. It comes down from the Father who created the heavenly lights. He doesn’t change like shadows that move.
God chose to give us new birth through the message of truth because he wanted us to be the first harvest of his new creation.

verses.heading: Listen to the Word and Do What It Says / Listen to the Word and Do What It Says
verses.text: My dear brothers and sisters, pay attention to what I say: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to get angry.
Human anger doesn’t produce the holy life God wants.
So get rid of everything that’s sinful and the evil that’s all around you, and humbly accept the word that’s planted in you, which can save you.
Don’t fool yourselves by just listening to the word. You also have to do what it says.
If someone listens to the word but doesn’t do what it says, they’re like a person who sees what they look like in a mirror
but then goes away and forgets what they saw.
But if someone takes a good look at the perfect law that gives freedom, if they keep looking at it and don’t forget what they’ve heard but do it, then that person will be blessed in what they do.
If someone thinks they’re religious, but they don’t control what they say, then they’re fooling themselves and their religion isn’t worth anything.
Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is to take care of widows and orphans who are in trouble and not let the world contaminate you.

verses.heading: Treat Everyone the Same / Treat Everyone the Same
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, believers in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ shouldn’t treat some people better than others.
Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and suppose a poor man in dirty old clothes also comes in.

Would you show special attention to the man wearing fine clothes? Would you tell him, “Here’s a good seat for you”? But would you say to the poor man, “You can stand over there,” or, “Sit on the floor by my feet”?
If you would, aren’t you treating some people better than others? Aren’t you like judges who have evil thoughts?

My dear brothers and sisters, listen to me. Hasn’t God chosen those who are poor in the world’s eyes to be rich in faith? Hasn’t he chosen them to receive the kingdom that he promised to give to those who love him?
But you haven’t treated poor people with respect. Isn’t it the rich who take advantage of you? Aren’t they the ones who drag you into court?
Aren’t they the ones who say insulting things about the worthy name of Jesus? Remember, you belong to him.
If you really keep the royal law that’s found in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as you love yourself,” you’ll be doing what’s right.
But if you treat some people better than others, that’s a sin, and the law will find you guilty as a law-breaker.
If you keep all the rest of the law but break one part of it, you’re guilty of breaking all of it.
The same one who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not commit murder.” If you don’t commit adultery but you do commit murder, then you’ve broken the law.
Speak and act like people who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom,
because anyone who hasn’t been merciful won’t receive mercy when they’re judged. But mercy wins out over judgment.

verses.heading: Show Your Faith by What You Do / Show Your Faith by What You Do
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, if a person claims to have faith but never acts on it, what good is that? Can that kind of faith save them?
Suppose a brother or a sister lacks clothes or food.
If one of you says to them, “I hope everything works out for you; stay warm and eat well,” but you don’t provide any practical help, what good is that?
It’s the same with faith. If it doesn’t lead us to take action, it’s dead.
But someone will say, “You have faith; I take action.” If you do have faith, the only way to show it is by the action it produces. But when I take action, that will show you the faith I have.
Do you have faith that there’s one God? Good for you! Even the demons believe that, and they tremble!
You foolish person, do you want proof that faith that doesn’t take action is useless?
When our father Abraham offered his son Isaac on the altar, wasn’t he considered to be right with God because he took action?
So you see that what he believed and the action he took were working together. His action made his faith complete.
And the Scripture came true that says, “Abraham believed God, and this was considered to make him right with God.” God even called Abraham his friend.
So you see that a person is considered right with God because of the action they take, not just because they believe.

In the same way, even Rahab the prostitute was considered to be right with God because of what she did for the spies. She gave them a place to stay and then sent them off safely in a different direction.
Just as a person’s body is dead without their spirit, so faith that doesn’t lead a person to act is dead.

verses.heading: Control What You Say / Control What You Say
verses.text: My brothers and sisters, most of you shouldn’t become teachers, because you know that those of us who do teach will be judged more strictly.
We all fail in many ways. If someone never says the wrong thing, then they’re a perfect person who’s able to keep their whole body under control.
We put a bit, a small metal bar, in the mouth of a horse to make it obey us, and we can control the whole animal with it.
To give another example, ships are very big, and they’re driven along by strong winds. But they can be steered by a very small rudder that makes them go wherever the captain wants to go.
In the same way, the tongue is a small part of a person’s body, but it brags about big things. Think how big a forest a small spark can set on fire.

The tongue is also a fire. It’s like an evil world of its own, right inside our bodies. It corrupts the entire body, and it sets a person’s whole life on fire, from start to finish. And the tongue itself is set on fire by hell.
People have tamed all kinds of wild animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures, and they still tame them.
But no one can tame the tongue. It’s a restless menace, full of deadly poison.
With our tongues we praise our Lord and Father, but with our tongues we also curse people who have been created to be like God.
Praise and cursing come out of the same mouth. My brothers and sisters, it shouldn’t be like that.
Can fresh water and salt water flow out of the same spring?
My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree produce olives, or can a grapevine produce figs? Of course not! A saltwater spring can’t produce fresh water either.

verses.heading: Two Kinds of Wisdom / Two Kinds of Wisdom
verses.text: If anyone among you is wise and understanding, they should show it by living a good life and doing things with the humility that comes from being wise.
But if you have bitterness, jealousy, and selfish ambition in your hearts, don’t be proud and pretend you’ve got the truth.
“Wisdom” like that doesn’t come down from above. It’s earthly, unspiritual, and demonic,
because wherever there’s jealousy and selfish ambition, there will also be chaos and all kinds of bad activity.
But the wisdom that comes from above is first pure, then peace-loving, kind, cooperative, full of mercy and good fruit, fair, and genuine.
People who make peace plant it like a seed, and they’ll harvest a crop of right living.

verses.heading: Obey God / Obey God
verses.text: Why do you fight and argue among yourselves? Isn’t it because of your wrong desires that fight within you?
You want something, but you don’t have it, so you kill. You want what others have, but you can’t get what you want, so you argue and fight. You don’t have what you want because you don’t ask God.
When you do ask for something, you don’t receive it because you’re asking for the wrong reason. You just want to satisfy your desires.
You unfaithful people, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Anyone who chooses to be the world’s friend becomes God’s enemy.
Scripture says with good reason that God wants the spirit he put in us to belong only to him.
But God gives us more grace, which is why Scripture says, “God opposes those who are proud, but he gives grace to those who are humble.”
So do what God wants. Resist the devil, and he’ll run away from you.
Come near to God, and he’ll come near to you. Wash your hands, you sinners, and make your hearts pure, you who can’t make up your minds.
Be full of sorrow, cry and weep, and change your laughter to mourning and your joy to sadness.
Approach the Lord humbly, and he will lift you up.

My brothers and sisters, don’t say bad things about one another. Anyone who says something bad about a brother or sister is saying it about the law, and anyone who judges another believer is judging the law. When you judge the law, you’re not keeping it, you’re acting as if you were its judge.
There’s only one Lawgiver and Judge, God, who is able to save life or destroy it. So who are you to judge your neighbor?

verses.heading: Bragging About Tomorrow / Bragging About Tomorrow
verses.text: Now listen, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we’re going to go to this or that city, spend a year there, buy and sell, and make money.”
You don’t even know what’s going to happen tomorrow. What is your life? You’re a mist that appears for a little while and then disappears.
Instead, you should say, “If it’s the Lord’s will, we will live and do this or that.”
As it is, you’re bragging about plans that you’ve made in your pride. That kind of bragging is wrong.
If anyone knows there’s something good they should do, but they don’t do it, that’s a sin for them.

verses.heading: A Warning to Rich People / A Warning to Rich People
verses.text: Listen, you rich people, cry and weep, because you’ll soon be suffering.
Your riches have rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes.
Your gold and silver have lost their brightness. Their dullness will be a witness against you and eat up your bodies like fire. You’ve kept all your money for yourself in these last days.

You’ve even failed to pay the workers who brought in your hay, and the money you owe them is now crying out against you. The cries of those who gathered your harvest have reached the ears of the Lord Almighty.
You’ve lived in luxury on earth and had everything you wanted. But you’ve only made yourselves fat like cattle to be butchered.
You’ve declared innocent people guilty and murdered them, even when they weren’t opposing you.

verses.heading: Be Patient When You Suffer / Be Patient When You Suffer
verses.text: Brothers and sisters, be patient until the Lord returns. See how the farmer waits for the land to produce its rich crop, being patient until the fall and spring rains come.
You too must be patient and stand firm, because the Lord will return soon.
Brothers and sisters, don’t complain about one another, because if you do, you’ll be judged. And the Judge is standing at the door!
Brothers and sisters, as an example of how to be patient when you suffer, think about the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
As you know, we consider people blessed who don’t give up. You’ve heard that Job was patient, and you’ve seen what the Lord finally did for him. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

Above all, my brothers and sisters, don’t swear any oaths, not by heaven or by the earth or by anything else. All you need to say is a simple “Yes” or “No.” If you do more than that, you’ll be found guilty.

verses.heading: The Prayer of Faith / The Prayer of Faith
verses.text: Is anyone among you in trouble? Then that person should pray. Is anyone among you happy? Then that person should sing songs of praise.
Is anyone among you sick? Then that person should send for the elders of the church to come and pray for them and anoint them with olive oil in the name of the Lord.
The prayer offered in faith will make the sick person well, and the Lord will heal them. If they’ve sinned, they’ll be forgiven.
So confess your sins to one another and pray for one another so that you will be healed. The prayer of a godly person is very powerful, and great things happen because of it.
Elijah was a human being just as we are. He prayed hard that it wouldn’t rain, and it didn’t rain on the land for three and a half years.
Then he prayed again and it did rain and the earth produced its crops.
My brothers and sisters, if one of you wanders away from the truth and someone else brings that person back,
remember that anyone who helps a sinner turn back from going the wrong way will save them from death and keep many sins from being discovered.
From Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ. To God’s chosen people, who are living away from their land. You’re scattered throughout the provinces of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.

God the Father knew you ahead of time, and he chose to make you pure and holy through the Spirit’s work. Then you would obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood to make you holy. May more and more grace and peace be given to you.

verses.heading: Peter Praises God for a Living Hope / Peter Praises God for a Living Hope
verses.text: May the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ be praised! In his great mercy he has given us a new birth into a living hope because Jesus Christ rose from the dead.
God has given us an inheritance that can never be destroyed, spoil, or fade away. It’s kept in heaven for us.
Through faith you are protected by God’s power until the coming of the salvation that will be revealed in the end.
You rejoice greatly because of all this, even though for a little while you may have had to suffer sadness in all kinds of troubles.

These have come to show that your faith is genuine. This will bring praise, honor, and glory to God when Jesus Christ returns. Your faith is worth even more than gold, because gold can be destroyed even after fire has made it pure.
Even though you’ve never seen Jesus, you love him. Though you don’t see him now, you believe in him and you’re filled with a glorious joy that can’t be put into words.
You’re receiving the salvation of your souls, which is the final result of your faith.
The prophets who spoke about the grace that was coming to you tried very hard and carefully to find out about this salvation.
The Spirit of Christ in them was telling about the sufferings of the Messiah and the glory that would follow. They wanted to find out when and how this salvation would come.

The prophets were shown that they weren’t serving themselves. Instead, they were serving you when they spoke about the things that you’ve now heard from those who preached the good news to you with the help of the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look into these things.

verses.heading: Be Holy / Be Holy
verses.text: So make sure your minds stay alert and completely sober. Put your hope in the grace that will be brought to you when Jesus Christ returns.
As obedient children, don’t give in to the wrong desires you had when you didn’t know any better.
God, who chose you, is holy. So you should be holy in all that you do.
It is written, “Be holy, because I am holy.”
You call on a Father who judges each person’s work without favoring one person over another. So live with the highest respect for God during your time as outsiders here.
You were set free from the empty way of life that was handed down to you by your own people from long ago. You know that you were not bought with things that can pass away, like silver or gold.
Instead, you were bought with the priceless blood of Christ. He was a perfect lamb without any flaws at all.
He was chosen before God created the world, and he was revealed for your sake in these last times.
Through him you believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory. So your faith and hope are in God.
You’ve made yourselves pure by obeying the truth. Now, you have an honest and true love for each other. So love one another deeply from your hearts.
You’ve been born again through the living word of God, which lasts forever. You haven’t been born again from a seed that will die, but from one that can’t die.
It is written, “All people are like grass, and all their glory is like the flowers in the field. The grass dries up and the flowers fall to the ground,
but the word of the Lord lasts forever.” And this is the word that was preached to you.
So get rid of all hatred, deceit, hypocrisy, jealousy, and insults of every kind.
Like newborn babies, you should crave the pure milk of God’s word. It will help you grow up as believers.
You will want to do this now that you have tasted how good the Lord is.

verses.heading: The Living Stone and a Chosen People / The Living Stone and a Chosen People
verses.text: Christ is the living Stone. People rejected him, but God chose him, and he’s very precious to God.

You’re also like living stones. As you come to Christ, you’re being built into a house for worship. There you will be holy priests and offer spiritual sacrifices that God will accept because of what Jesus Christ has done.
In Scripture it says, “Look! I’m placing a stone in Zion, a chosen and precious cornerstone. The one who trusts in him will never be put to shame.”
This stone is precious to you who believe. But to people who don’t believe, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.”
And, “It’s a stone that causes people to trip, a rock that makes them fall.” People who don’t obey the message trip and fall, just the way God planned it.

But God chose you to be his own people, his royal priests, a holy nation, his special treasure. You’re all these things so that you can tell everyone how wonderful God is. He brought you out of darkness and into his marvelous light.
Once you weren’t a people, but now you are the people of God. Once you hadn’t received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

verses.heading: Living Godly Lives Among People Who Don’t Believe / Living Godly Lives Among People Who Don’t Believe
verses.text: Dear friends, in this world you’re outsiders who are living away from their land. So don’t give in to your wrong desires, which fight against your soul.
People who don’t believe might accuse you of doing wrong. But lead such good lives among them that they’ll see your good deeds and give glory to God on the day Jesus returns.
For the Lord’s sake, follow the lead of every human authority. Obey the emperor, who is the highest authority.
Also obey the governors that the emperor sends to punish people who do wrong and praise those who do right.
By doing good, you’ll stop to the talk of foolish people who don’t know what they’re saying. This is what God wants you to do.
Live as free people, but don’t use your freedom to cover up evil. Live as people who are God’s slaves.
Show proper respect to everyone, love the family of believers, have respect for God, honor the emperor.
Slaves, obey your masters out of deep respect for God. Obey those who are good and kind, but also obey also those who aren’t kind.
If a person is punished unfairly and they take it patiently because they want to obey God, they deserve to be praised for that.

But if a person is punished for doing wrong and they take it patiently, they don’t deserve any special praise. But if you do suffer for doing good and you put up with it, God will praise you for that.
This is what God wants you to do. Remember, Christ suffered for you, and he left you an example that he expects you to follow.
Scripture says, “He didn’t commit any sin. No lies ever came out of his mouth.”

People shouted at him and insulted him, but he didn’t do the same thing back to them. He didn’t threaten to get revenge against the people who were making him suffer. Instead, he trusted in God, who judges fairly.
“He himself carried our sins” in his body on the cross. He did that so, free from sins, we would lead godly lives. “His wounds have healed you.”
“You were like sheep wandering away.” But now you have returned to the Shepherd who watches over your souls.
Wives, follow the lead of your own husbands. If any of them don’t believe God’s word, they may be won over to Christ without words by seeing how their wives live.
Let them see that your lives are pure and full of respect for God.

Let them see a beauty in you that comes from the inside, not from the outside. Your beauty shouldn’t come from fancy hairstyles or gold jewelry or expensive clothes. Instead, it should be the inner beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit. Beauty like that doesn’t fade away. God considers it very valuable.
That’s how the holy women of the past used to make themselves beautiful when they put their hope in God and followed the lead of their own husbands.
Sarah was like that. She obeyed Abraham and even called him her master. You’ll be like her if you do what’s right and don’t give in to fear.

Husbands, be understanding of your wives. Treat them with respect, remembering the ways in which they’re physically weaker than you. Honor them as people who will share the gracious gift of life with you. Otherwise, God won’t answer your prayers.

verses.heading: Suffering for Doing Good / Suffering for Doing Good
verses.text: Finally, I want all of you to agree with one another. Be understanding, love one another, be kind and tender, be humble.
If someone does something wrong to you or insults you, don’t do the same thing to them. Instead, respond with kind words. This is what God wants you to do so that you can receive a blessing.
Scripture says, “If anyone wants to love life and see good days, they must keep their tongue from speaking evil and their lips from telling lies.
They must turn away from evil and do good, and they must look for peace and go after it.
The Lord keeps his eyes on godly people, and his ears are open to their prayers, but the Lord opposes those who do evil.”
Who’s going to hurt you if you really want to do good?
But if you suffer for doing what’s right, even then you’ll be blessed. Scripture says, “Don’t fear their threats and don’t be afraid.”
But make sure that you honor Christ as Lord in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to anyone who asks you to give a reason for the hope you have. But do this gently and with respect.
Keep your conscience clear, so that even if people say bad things about you as believers in Christ, they’ll be ashamed when the way you live proves them wrong.
If it’s God’s will for you to suffer for doing good, that’s better than suffering for doing wrong.
Christ also suffered once for sins. Someone who did right suffered for those who did wrong, in order to bring you to God. Jesus was put to death in the body, but he was made alive in the Spirit.
Then he went and told the good news to the spirits who were being held in prison.
These were the spirits of those who had disobeyed long before, when God was being patient while Noah built the ark. Only a few people, eight in all, were saved from the flood in the ark.

The water of the flood is a picture of the way that baptism now saves you too. It doesn’t save you by washing the dirt off your body. Instead, it’s your way of promising God that you’ll keep a clear conscience by the same power that raised Jesus Christ from the dead.
He has now gone into heaven, and he’s at God’s right hand, with angels, authorities, and powers under his control.

verses.heading: Living for God / Living for God
